13. Now, the meditation on the person who is the presiding deity of Mercury:
he should be visualized as a human form, golden in color, four-armed, and holding a conch, a discus, a mace, and a lotus.
He is golden-colored. || 1 || 1 ||
14. Now, the meditation on Bṛhaspati:

O Blessed Bṛhaspati, preceptor of all the gods, of the Āṅgirasa lineage, lord of the Sindhu region, with arms shining like glowing gold, four-armed, with hands marked by the staff, water-pot, rosary, and the gesture of granting boons, clad in yellow garments, garlands, and unguents, beautiful with ornaments of topaz, sovereign of all sciences—salutations to you! Adorned with a bound yellow banner, mounted upon a chariot drawn by eight horses, come circling Mount Meru clockwise; together with Indra and Brahmā, occupy the middle of the northern petal of the lotus upon a long, square, golden throne, facing north. One should meditate upon him along with his limbs, weapons, retinue, consort, and power.
He was joined by eight white horses in a golden chariot.
Bṛhaspati indeed remains in each zodiac sign for one year. || 1 ||
For the purification of the preceptors of the gods and daityas, [the two images] are yellow and white, each with four arms.
The two [deities] should be depicted holding staffs and granting boons, and carrying rosaries and water-pots.
Golden-hued. || 1 ||
15. Now, the meditation on the Guru as the presiding deity and Indra:
Mounted upon a four-tusked elephant, his excellent hands hold a thunderbolt and a goad.
The Lord of the East (Indra) should be fashioned, adorned with various ornaments.
He is golden-colored. || 1 ||
16. Now, the meditation on the Guru as the presiding deity Brahmā:

One should contemplate Brahmā, seated upon a lotus throne, with matted hair and four faces, holding a rosary, a sacrificial ladle (*sruva*), a book, and a water-pot (*kamaṇḍalu*); clothed in a black antelope skin, with a swan standing at his side.
The color of the *pāṭala* flower. || 1 ||
17. Now, the meditation on semen (śukradhyāna):

O Blessed One, Bhārgava, preceptor of all the Daityas, of the Bhārgava lineage, Lord of the land of Bhojakaṭa, O you whose limbs are as radiant as silver, four-armed one, whose hands are marked with the staff, water-pot, rosary, and the gesture of granting boons, clad in white garments, garlands, and unguents, whose entire body is adorned with diamond ornaments, whose intellect is proficient in all the treatises on ethics—salutations to you! Adorned with a white banner, mounted upon a chariot drawn by eight white horses, come while circumambulating Mount Meru; together with Indrāṇī and Indra, occupy the center of the eastern petal of the lotus upon a five-cornered pedestal, facing east. One should meditate upon him along with his limbs, weapons, retinue, consort, and power.
The chariot, complete with its protective fender, was yoked to horses born of the earth.
The great chariot, however, was white, equipped with quivers and banners. || 1 ||
For the purification of the preceptors of the gods and daityas, they are yellow and white, each with four arms.
The two [deities] should be depicted as holding staffs, granting boons, and possessing rosaries and water-pots.
White in color. || 1 ||
18. Now, the meditation on Indrāṇī, the presiding deity of Śukra:
In the hand of the consort of Indra (Indrāṇī), there should be a gentle cluster of *saṃtāna* blossoms.
Abhayā, Āmaṇḍitā, Akāryā, Vibhujā, and likewise Śacī. || 1 ||
Golden-hued. || 1 ||
19. Now, the meditation on Indra, the presiding deity of Śukra:
[One should meditate on him] mounted upon a white elephant, with his hands skillfully holding a thunderbolt and a goad.
I meditate upon Indra, who has a thousand eyes and a yellow luster, within my heart. || 1 ||
Golden-colored. || 1 ||
20. Now, the meditation on Śanaiścara:

O Blessed One, Śanaiścara, son of Bhāskara, of the Kāśyapa lineage, Lord of the Saurāṣṭra country, whose body has a luster like collyrium; four-armed one, with hands marked by the bow, arrow, sword, and the gesture of fearlessness; clad in blue garments, garlands, and unguents; whose entire body is adorned with ornaments of blue gems; embodiment of wrath that terrifies all the worlds—salutations to you! Adorned with a fastened blue banner, mounted upon a chariot drawn by eight blue vultures, come circling Mount Meru clockwise! Together with Prajāpati and Yama, occupy the middle of the western petal of the lotus, facing westward, seated upon a bow-shaped pedestal, and meditate upon [the deity] along with his limbs, weapons, retinue, consort, and power.
Having the luster of sapphire, holding a sword, bestowing boons, and having a vulture as his vehicle.
The heroic son of the Sun (Rāhu) should always be made to hold arrows and a bow.
He is dark-complexioned. || 1 ||
21. Now, the meditation on Prajāpati, the presiding deity of Śani:
he should be visualized as mounted upon a swan-vehicle, and he should not be depicted with four faces.
The auspicious Sāvitrī should be depicted on his left lap.
The supreme task spoken by Brahmā is the entire form of Prajāpati.
Wearing the sacred thread, seated upon a swan, he has one face and four arms.
He holds a rosary of beads, a sacrificial ladle, a water-pot, and likewise a book.
The color of a lotus. || 1 ||
22. Now, the meditation on Yama, the presiding deity of Saturn: Yama has blood-red eyes, holds a noose in his hand, and has a buffalo for his vehicle.
Kāla has a terrifying face, a dark-blue body, and is exceedingly fearsome.
Blue in color. || 1 ||
23. Now, the meditation on Rāhu:

O Blessed One, Rāhu, crusher of the sun and moon, delight of Siṃhikā, of the Paiṭhīnasi lineage, Lord of the Barbarian lands, with the luster of a dark cloud, tiger-faced, four-armed, with hands marked by the sword, shield, trident, and the gesture of granting boons, clad in black garments, garlands, and unguents, all your limbs adorned with ornaments of *gomeda* stone, O treasure-house of valor, salutations to you! Accompanied by your black banner fully prepared, riding upon your vehicle, the chariot of a black lion, circumambulating Mount Meru, come here; together with Sarpa and Kāla, occupy the leaden image facing south in the middle of the lotus petal of Nairṛta upon a winnowing-basket-shaped pedestal—thus one should meditate upon you, complete with your limbs, weapons, retinue, consort, and power.
With a formidable face, he holds a sword, a shield, and a trident, and bestows boons.
And Rāhu, seated upon a blue lion-throne, bestows auspiciousness upon me. || 1 ||
The color of a dark blue cloud. || 1 ||
24. Now, the meditation on the serpents who are the presiding deities of Rāhu:
the serpents hold rosaries and are adorned with water-pots and tails.
They have either one enjoyment or three enjoyments, and all their activities are terrifying. || 1 ||
Red in color. || 1 ||
25. Now, the meditation on Kāla, the presiding deity of Rāhu:
Kāla has a terrifying countenance, his body is blue, and he is exceedingly fearsome.
He should be depicted holding a noose and a staff, with hair like that of a snake or a scorpion.
He is black in color. || 1 ||
p.
127) 26 Now, the meditation on the banner (ketudhyāna):

"O Lord Ketu, of the form of smoke, of the Jaimini lineage, Lord of the Middle Country, having the appearance of a smoke-colored banner, two-armed, with hands marked by the mace and the gesture of granting boons, adorned with variegated garlands and unguents, all your limbs decorated with excellent ornaments of lapis lazuli, O you of wondrous power! Salutations to you! Adorned with a fastened and variegated banner, mounted upon a chariot drawn by variegated pigeons, come while circumambulating Mount Meru from the left! Together with Brahmā and Citragupta, occupy the middle of the western petal of the lotus, presiding over a bell-metal image facing south upon a pedestal in the shape of a banner. One should meditate [upon him] along with his limbs, weapons, retinue, consort, and power."
All were smoke-colored, bringing happiness, bearing maces, and having various distorted forms.
Those whose banners always have a pigeon as their vehicle shall be granters of boons.
All the planets, which bring welfare to the world, should be depicted wearing crowns.
(Although there are many comets, only one is preeminent: They are smoke-colored. || 1 ||

27. Now, the meditation on Brahmā as the presiding deity of the Ketu [asterism]—(according to the Śaiva Āgama): One should meditate upon Viriñci, the Lord of Speech, seated upon a white lotus, possessing great luster.
I should meditate upon him with a rosary, a water-pot, the gesture of protection, and a hand in the act of giving. || 1 ||
The color of a lotus. || 1 ||
28. Now, the meditation on Citragupta, the presiding deity of the Ketu constellation—(according to Bhaṭṭabhāskara):
He has a charming appearance, a beautiful form, two arms, and a gentle countenance.
In her right hand she holds a pen, and in her left a leaf.
One should visualize Citragupta, whose beard, hair, and eyes are tawny.
Golden-colored. || 1 ||
Now, the meditation on the deities who ensure the perfection of the ritual action—29. First among these is the meditation on Durgā (according to the Śaiva Āgama):
[One should meditate on] Durgā, adorned with eight arms, for the destruction of calamity.
I meditate upon that slayer of Daityas, who is red in hue and intent on devouring [them]. || 1 ||
She is blue in color. || 1 ||
30. Now, the meditation on Gaṇapati (from the Śaivāgama):
[One should meditate upon him] as having a single tusk, an elephant face, a trunk, and being fond of modaka sweets.
I bow my head in reverence to Śūrpakarṇa, who stands upon the back of a rat.
He is red in color. || 1 ||
p.
128) 31 Now, the meditation on Kṣetrapāla—(in the *Kāraṇāgama*):
One should meditate on Kṣetrapāla as being of dark complexion, with a face contorted by a frown.
He has three eyes, hair standing erect, is exceedingly wrathful, and possesses prominent fangs.
With feet adorned by anklets and decorated with serpent chains;
His ankles were bound with small bells, and he was adorned with a garland of skulls.
He has a serpent as his sacred thread, wears the moon upon his crest, and is clothed only by the directions.
On the right, he holds a trident, a vetāla, a sword, and a drum.
And in his left hands, he bears a skull-cup, a bell, a shield, and a bow.
I salute Kṣetrapāla for the pacification of all misfortunes. || 4 ||
Dark-complexioned. || 1 ||
32. Now, the meditation on the Bestower of Fearlessness (from the Śaiva Āgama): [It is] the destroyer of the multitude of fears for the throngs of bowing people.
I praise him who bestows fearlessness and who constantly grants happiness.
Golden-hued. (All else is like Indra; 4th initiation. || 1 ||
33. Now, the meditation on the Vāstupuruṣa (according to the Śaiva Āgama): [One should meditate on him] as the purifier of the ground, holding a measuring rod in his lotus-hand.
I pay homage to the Vāstupuruṣa, who lies upon his auspicious bed. || 1 ||
Blue in color; two-armed. (1)
34. Now, the meditation on Mṛtyuñjaya (in the Śaivāgama):
[One should meditate on Him] who stands in the center of a blossoming lotus, with the moon, sun, and fire as His eyes.
His splendor was moistened by the nectar dripping from the moon bound upon his crest.
Holding a mudrā, a noose, a book, and a rosary.
We worship the Lord Īśāna, the conqueror of death, who removes the suffering of his devotees. || 2 ||
White in color. || 1 ||
35. Now, the natures of the four yugas—(from the Padma Purāṇa):
"In this way, O King, the Kṛta and the other ages have bull-faced lords."
They resemble a well-ripened mango, flax flowers, blue lotuses, and parrots. || 1 ||
They were all radiant, adorned with fine garments, excellent flowers, and ornaments.
All of them indeed hold a conch and a lotus, and their hands are in the gestures of granting boons and fearlessness. || 2 || 4 ||
36. Therein, the nature of the Kali-puruṣa is described in the Śrī Viṣṇu Purāṇa (Book 1, Chapter 16): "A Śūdra wearing the insignia of a king, killing a pair of cattle with his foot."
Another method.
And he saw the low-born man, marked with the insignia of royalty, holding a staff in his hand; he was dark-complexioned. (1st Skandha, 17th Chapter) [He was] black in color. (1)
p. 129) 37. Now, the meditation on the presiding deities of the four ages (*caturyuga-abhimānidevatā-dhyāna*)—(from the *Padmapurāṇa*):
In the Kṛta age it is white, in the Tretā it is reddish, and likewise in the Dvāpara.
Vāsudeva, the primordial Person, is yellow, dark as a mass of clouds, and resides before [all]. || 1 ||
Holding, respectively, the conch, the Śārṅga bow, the mace, and the discus with her arms.
Seated comfortably with beautiful hands, they are the presiding deities of the Yugas. || 2 || 4 ||
Now, the forms of the sixty-year cycle beginning with Prabhava—(from the *Kāraṇāgama*, *Madanaratna*, *Horā*):
38. First, the form of the year Prabhava: he has two feet, bears a tilaka mark on his forehead, and is black in complexion.
And the man who is a Brāhmaṇa by birth has bloodshot eyes and a stout body. || 1 ||
He is black in color. || 1 ||
39. Now, the nature of the Vibhava year: [The deity] wears a garland made of jewels and pearls upon his neck.
One should meditate upon such a magnificent being, adorned with divine armlets and mounted upon a chariot. || 1 ||
Meghavarṇa || 1 ||
40. Now, the nature of the White Year (Śuklasaṃvatsara): It is covered with divine unguents and adorned with white garments.
Beneath the Lipikalpadruma, one should meditate upon the year known as Śukla. || 1 ||
White in color. || 1 ||
41. Now, the nature of the Pramoda year:
He has five faces, a most fierce form, rolling eyes, and bears a dark-blue complexion.
He should be known as one whose body is embraced by his beloved, overflowing with joy.
He is dark-complexioned. || 1 ||
42. Now, the nature of Prajāpati-Saṃvatsara:
he resembles the blazing fire of time (Kālānala), with his hands granting boons and fearlessness.
Mahodara, Lohitākṣa, Vatsara, and Prajāvatī. || 1 ||
Red in color. || 1 ||
43. Now, the nature of the Āṅgirasa year:
between the eyebrows and the eyes, it is wheel-shaped and white in luster.
One should meditate upon the deity named Āṅgirasa, who has two hands holding lotuses. || 1 ||
White in color. || 1 ||
p. 130) 44. Now, the nature of the Śrīmukha year:
it is covered with many jewels and possesses a neck thick with saliva.
One should meditate upon Śrīmukhavatsara, who has lotus-like eyes and the complexion of turmeric.
Golden-hued. || 1 ||
45. Now, the nature of the Bhāva-saṃvatsara:
it is characterized by an insentient state, and likewise, the hand and the sign of Capricorn (Mṛga) are the ascendant.
And one with both arms raised is known as a Kṣatriya. || 1 ||
Red in color. || 1 ||
46. Now, the nature of the Youthful Year (yuvasaṃvatsara):
it is fashioned like the [peacock] of Garuḍa, with side-glances that are blue lotuses of laughter.
He has two arms, is white in color, has lotus-seed eyes, and is like a youth in his prime. || 1 ||
White in color. || 1 ||
47. Now, the nature of the Dhātusaṃvatsara:
the deity holds a lotus in his hand and resembles Mount Kailāsa.
Three-eyed, lotus-colored, fearless, and known as the Element (dhātu). || 1 ||
The color of a lotus. || 1 ||
48. Now, the nature of the Īśvara-year:
[He is] resplendent like a thousand rising suns, two-armed, and facing the upward direction.
One should meditate upon the Lord known as Īśvara, who wears variegated garments. || 1 ||
The color is reddish-orange. || 1 ||

49. Now, the nature of the Bahudhanya year: [The deity] has a jar of nectar in his hand, his body is filled with splendor, he is worshipped by all the gods, and his sole concern is the Vedas and the Shastras.
With broad and beautiful radiance, a long chest, and two feet, he possesses lotus-like eyes; when twelve years have been meditated upon, [he appears]. || 1 ||
Blue in color. || 1 ||
50. Now, the nature of the Pramāthin year:
he is most righteous, fair-complexioned, long-chested, and well-proportioned.
A man wearing a necklace of rubies is the Pramāthin year. || 1 ||
Golden-hued. || 1 ||
51. Now, the nature of the Vikrama Saṃvatsara:
[the deity] has dark eyes, is skilled in the arts, has the complexion of wheat, and speaks for one's welfare.
They know his stride to be of medium height, with long arms and the gait of an elephant. || 1 ||
The color of wheat. || 1 ||
52. Now, the nature of the Viṣu-saṃvatsara:
The one named Viṣu-saṃvatsara has a dark-blue body and is devoted to ritual placement (nyāsa).
With eyes like those of a mouse-eater, his mouth was scarred and he was unsteady. || 1 ||
Blue in color. || 1 ||
53. Now, the nature of the Citrabhānu year:
he has two arms, is hunchbacked, dark-complexioned, and endowed with upright hair.
Adorned with various ornaments, he stayed in a temple at the place of recitation.
The color is tawny. || 1 ||
54. Now, the nature of the Svabhānu year:
Kapila is of cruel disposition and is adorned with red garments.
Afflicted by thirst, he has the face of a ram; he is self-luminous, two-armed, and all-pervading. || 1 ||
He is of a tawny color. || 1 ||
55. Now, the nature of the Tāraṇa year:
[the deity] has a beautiful and tall body, and is skilled in the arts of dance and instrumental music.
Nīrajākṣa shall be Vyāghrapāt, and he who is named Tāraṇa shall be Gajāsyas. || 1 ||
Red in color. || 1 ||
56. Now, the nature of the Pārthiva year:
[its deity] is an ascetic, fair-complexioned, long-necked, and large-bellied.
And a king who inflicts punishment upon thieves is remembered as one who is grossly deceitful. || 1 ||
He is fair-complexioned. || 1 ||
57. Now, the nature of the Vyaya year:
it has a long face, a dark luster, and red eyes, hair, and beard.
He is skillful, truthful in speech, and a man who knows how to manage his expenditures.
The color is tawny. || 1 ||
58. Now, the nature of the Sarvajit year:
it has a long nose and face, is heroic, has thin lips, and is fair-complexioned.
He is the one who possesses faith, the digger of the well, the all-conquering, and the accomplisher of all. || 1 ||
He is fair-complexioned. || 1 ||
59. Now, the nature of the Sarvadhārī year:
he resides in a village that is not large, has keen vision, and is a farmer.
He has subtle lips and a long body, and he is the sustainer of all at all times. || 1 ||
He is red in color. || 1 ||
60. Now, regarding the nature of the adverse years (*virodhisaṃvatsara*):
namely, Taskara, Hiṃsaka, Āmlabhuj, and Mandalocana.
He has a slender neck and a large body, with a thick middle; he is the one who is antagonistic. || 1 ||
Red in color. || 1 ||
61. Now, the nature of the Vikṛti year:
he has a beautiful and tall body, is an ascetic, and is fair-complexioned.
A man with a withered belly and a long neck, red eyes, and a deformed appearance. || 1 ||
He is fair-complexioned. || 1 ||
62. Now, the nature of the Kharasaṃvatsara:
the Khara [year] is situated with four arms in a temple or on a riverbank.
The supreme one has his hands in the gestures of granting boons and fearlessness, and he holds a mace and a lotus. || 1 ||
He is red in color. || 1 ||
63. Now, the nature of the Naṇdana year:
he has red eyes, long arms, and is endowed with a long nose.
A man who is endowed with sacred ash and rudrākṣa beads becomes a granter of boons and a source of delight. || 1 ||
Red in color. || 1 ||
64. Now, the nature of the Vijaya year:
the male deity has two arms, resembles a lotus, and is equipped with an arrow and a bow.
The gaze directed toward the left and all around is the Vijaya [mudrā], which originates from the root of Arjuna. || 1 ||
The color of a lotus. || 1 ||
65. Now, the nature of the Jaya year:
he has two arms, thick hips, and is endowed with red eyes.
And Jayā is white, with hands granting boons and fearlessness, joined with Śyāmā. || 1 ||
Smoke-colored. || 1 ||
66. Now, the nature of the Manmatha year:
[The deity is] a person with lotus-eyes, rounded arms, and holding an arrow and a bow.
Mounted upon the fivefold submarine fire, the God of Love is the creator of passion. || 1 ||
Golden-colored. || 1 ||
67. Now, the nature of the year Durmukhi: His face is formidable with fangs, and his splendor resembles the rising moon.
He has two arms, holds the Śārṅga bow in his hand, has a fierce countenance, and delights in a fierce countenance.
White in color.
68. Now, regarding the nature of the Hemalamba and Vilamba years: Hemalamba and Vilamba are red-eyed, cruel, and agitated.
Those two were red in color, aged, and always remained in the presence of the Mothers.
The two are red in color. || 2 ||
69. Now, regarding the nature of the Vikārī-Śārvari year:
Vikārī, Śārvarī, Bhṛśuṇḍī, and Musalāyudhā.
And the two, resembling mountains, were seated at the foot of a tree known as the Śiṃśupā.
The two [deities] are red in color. || 2 ||
70. Now, the nature of the *plava* year:
one who is always situated on a boat by the shore of the ocean, traveling to other islands.
He is skilled in the protection of horses, agile, and possesses the speed of a leaping deer. || 1 ||
He is red in color. || 1 ||
71. Now, regarding the nature of the years Śubhakṛt and Śobhakṛt:
Śubhakṛt and Śobhakṛt indeed have the appearance of old men in the forest.
Wearing lotus and rudrākṣa beads, they resembled sandalwood trees.
The two are red in color. || 2 ||
72. Now, the nature of the Krodhi year:
[the deity] is completely enveloped by tigers, fearful by nature, and afflicted by hunger.
Meditating upon Śiva and Nārāyaṇa, he was short, white-complexioned, and prone to anger.
White in color. || 1 ||
73. Now, the nature of the Viśvāvasu year: the man who dwells upon the ground in a waterless forest is Viśvāvasu.
Resorting to the steps of the pond, he indeed meditated upon the one whose face is turned in every direction. || 1 ||
He is red in color. || 1 ||
74. Now, regarding the nature of the Parābhava and Plavaṅga years:
Parābhava and Plavaṅga [arose] in the vicinity of Śveta and Puṣkara.
One remains stationary while the other leaps; both young men are full of pride.
They are white in color. || 2 ||
75. Now, regarding the nature of the Kīlaka and Saumya years: the two youths, Nīla and Lohita, having placed the moon upon their heads...
Kīlaka and Saumya were performing austerities on the slope of the mountain.
The two colors are blue and red. || 2 ||
76. Now, the nature of the Sādhāraṇa year: The Sādhāraṇa [year] is on the bank of the Sarasvatī, surrounded by a multitude of brahmins.
The twice-born dwells there, worshipping the Lord Īśāna from the front.
Golden-hued. || 1 ||
77. Now, the nature of the Virodhikṛt year:
Virodhikṛt is of cruel deeds, equipped with bow and arrow, and is night.
With blood-red eyes and a massive body, he wanders about killing deer. || 1 ||
Blue in color. || 1 ||
78. Now, the nature of the Paridhāvī year:
[the deity] wears a deer-skin as a head-covering, carries a bow, has squinting eyes, and is deceitful.
Wearing sandals, he wandered through the forest, hunting deer as he ran about.
White in color. || 1 ||
79. Now, the nature of the year for one who is negligent: with arms raised, he dwells by the bank of a forest river, smeared with ashes.
One who meditates on the sun, one who is emaciated, one who is dark-complexioned, one who is negligent, and one who is twice-born (a Brahmin) are thus described. || 1 ||
Blue in color.
80. Now, the nature of the Ānanda year:
having applied the *ūrdhvapuṇḍra* mark, remaining composed, and dwelling in a solitary forest;
Ānanda was red in complexion, meditating, and adorned with a rosary of beads. || 1 ||
Red in color. || 1 ||
81. Now, the nature of the Rākṣasa year:
[The person born in this year] carries a thick staff on his shoulder, holds a stone in his hand, and wanders in the forest.
But the Rākṣasa, whose mouth was like that of a dog, was harassing travelers. || 1 ||
Blue in color.
82. Now, the nature of the Nala-year:
[The Lord] stands in the midst of the water of ascetics, clothed in bark and the skin of a black antelope.
Wearing matted locks, with a dark complexion, peaceful, and adorned with sacred ashes. || 1 ||
He is black in color. || 1 ||
83. Now, regarding the nature of Piṅgalaka and Kālayukti as the two years:
Piṅgala and Kālayukti have red faces and red eyes.
While chanting prayers in the forest near a neem tree, he beheld one with white and blue limbs.
White in color. || 2 || Blue in color. || 2 ||
84. Now, the nature of the Siddhārtha year:
having bathed at twilight on the seashore, facing the sun;
A student (brahmacārī) who stands, meditates, and recites [mantras] for a year becomes white like a sword-blade. || 1 ||
White in color. || 1 ||
85. Now, the nature of the Raudri year: King Raudri is seated upon the throne and is deceitful.
He has red eyes and a stout body; he is dark-complexioned and delights in playing with dice. || 1 ||
He is black in color. || 1 ||
86. Now, the nature of the Durmati year:
Durmati is a Kṣatriya, brave, stout, and has a horse as his vehicle.
Wielding a sword and shield, he is blood-red and eager to sever his enemies. || 1 ||
He is red in color. || 1 ||
87. Now, the nature of the Dundubhi year:
having reached Puṣkaradvīpa, Dundubhi [resides] in the vicinity of the Plakṣa tree.
Meditating thus, he dwells without fear, truly contemplating Viṣṇu, who possesses the universal form.
Blue in color. || 1 ||
88. Now, the nature of the year Rudhirodgārī: he who is named Rudhirodgārī dwells on the bank of the Puṣkara lake.
One should worship Rudra, who consists of eleven forms, with *droṇa* flowers.
Golden-colored. || 1 ||
89. Now, the nature of the Raktākṣi year:
Residing in a golden palace, in a pavilion near the ocean.
The Lord, his limbs adorned, was sporting with women; he was youthful and had red eyes. || 1 ||
White in color. || 1 ||
90. Now, the nature of the Krodhana year:
Krodhana has a crooked form, red limbs, and resides near a tree.
Playing with dogs, his eyes darting restlessly, he was wrathful and had a distorted face. || 1 ||
Red in color. || 1 ||
91. Now, the nature of the inexhaustible year (akṣayasaṃvatsara):
Having reached Śālmalidvīpa, he dwells upon a seat of stone.
He was cruel, dark-complexioned, with long hair, imperishable, tall in stature, and masculine. || 1 ||
Black in color. || 1 ||
136) Now, the names of the *idvatsara* and others—(from the *Kālamādhavīya*):

*idvatsara*, *iḍāvatsara*, *saṃvatsara*, *parivatsara*, and *anuvatsara*. These designations are to be understood as applying respectively to each group of five among the first fifty years of the sixty-year cycle beginning with *prabhava*. || 5 ||

92. Now, the characteristics of those born in the sixty-year cycle beginning with Prabhava—(from the *Jātakābharaṇa*): First, regarding *Prabhava*: one who delights in the accumulation of all things, possesses a continuous lineage of sons, and is exceedingly wise.
That man is born endowed with all enjoyments and long life, arising from great power. || 1 ||
In the *vibhava* [year], one is a consumer of what has arisen, pleasant to behold, endowed with strength and other virtues, clever, and skilled in the arts (*kalā*).
A man born in the year of Jupiter (Vibhava) shall become a king in his own family, being virtuous and learned.
In the Śukla [dasa], he is always exceedingly joyful, noble, accompanied by virtuous sons and wife, and endowed with prosperity.
A man endowed with good fortune, knowledge, and discipline is surely born from the Śukla [family]. || 1 ||
(Prāmodyate) — The donor, endowed with constant joy, beloved, eternally possessed of truth, and virtuous, shall be successful.
He is skillful, clever, a performer of others' tasks, a source of joy, a younger brother, and full of self-respect.
(In the case of the birth of a daughter:

A mortal born as a ruler of subjects would be exceedingly proud of his generosity, compassionate, following the traditions of his lineage, possessed of charming character, devoted to the worship of gods and Brahmins, and humble. || 1 ||
(Regarding Āṅgīrasa:
He will be handsome, happy, endowed with enjoyments, dignified, a speaker of pleasant words, and possessed of many sons.
Indeed, a person whose intellect is well-guarded shall be long-lived and free from disease for as many years as there are syllables in the speech of Aṅgiras. || 1 ||
(At Śrīmukha:
He is illustrious, powerful, a knower of many scriptures, dear to his friends, possessed of beautiful intellect, and exceedingly strong.
A man born under Śrīmukha will be exceedingly noble, endowed with good reputation, and possessed of great generosity. || 1 ||
(In the case of the state of being: one who is highly praiseworthy in mind, exceedingly illustrious, endowed with virtues, possessed of fortitude, and humble.
One who is always full of joy and free from dispute would possess a sense of self-arising from the expression of many states of being. || 1 ||
(To the youth:
He is of pleasing form, virtuous, self-restrained, peaceful, and exceedingly devoted to giving.
In the year of Puruṣa, a man becomes wise, long-lived, possessing a firm body, and full of contentment. || 1 ||
In that realm,
even Śakra, endowed with reverence for all the virtues of the world, was exceedingly devoted to his guru.
One born in the year of the Ox should be skilled in the arts and sciences, virtuous in conduct, and free from disease. || 1 ||
137) (In the case of Īśvara:
one who has experienced great wrath arising at that moment, devoid of joy, yet virtuous and majestic.
O Lord, a mortal who is born under this asterism becomes skillful, endowed with proficiency in the arts, and possessed of virtuous character. || 1 ||
Skilled in many activities, honored by the king, proud of his generosity, and indeed a knower of the scriptures.
A man born under Bahudhānya will indeed possess abundant grain and wealth in many ways and of many kinds. || 1 ||
(Prāmāthinī) —
He is endowed with chariots, banners, umbrellas, horses, and so forth, and is a slayer of those devoted to the scriptures.
A man born in the Pramāthin year shall become the grateful minister of a king.
(Vikrama)—
He is intensely devoted to exceedingly fierce deeds and is highly skilled in the crushing of the circle of his enemies.
He is a hero, exceedingly brave, noble, and powerful, born with the rain of valor. || 1 ||
O Sage, he is indeed powerful, yet of blameworthy character; he follows the wicked and performs the tasks of others.
In the year of the Bull, a man becomes talkative, fond of many women, lazy, and excessively greedy. || 1 ||
To Citrabhānu—
whose mind is solely intent upon variegated garments and flowers, and who is ever accompanied by Mānasodbhavā.
For a person born from the Fire-god (Citrabhānu) is indeed adorned with beautiful conduct and radiant arts. || 1 ||
(Svabhāni)— One with curly hair who is upright, of beautiful luster, having conquered the faction of enemies, wise, and humble.
A man born in the year Svabhānu will have a serene form and be summoned by equal success. || 1 ||
(Tāraṇe)— He is cunning, brave, fickle, skilled in the arts, utterly cruel, and a performer of censurable deeds.
The man born in the month of Tāraṇa shall be liberated from the wealth of one who enjoys what has been produced. || 1 ||
(The king)— being intensely devoted to his own duty and action, has attained the state of having reached the further shore of good conduct.
One who is skilled in the entire range of arts and full of grace will become a noble king in the year of Pārthiva. || 1 ||
In the house of expenditure (the twelfth), one who is overcome by calamities and devoid of happiness is afraid and does not repay even a small amount of debt.
A man born [in this position] has an unstable disposition of mind and is habitually engaged in expenditure and wasteful activities. || 1 || 20 ||
(Sarvajit)— a great festival honoring the king, pure, human, broad-bodied, and of great splendor.
The man born in the month of Śarad is always intent on conquering the host of enemies and is a victor over all. || 1 ||
(Sarvadhāriṇī)—
Possessed of prosperity, servants, and many enjoyments, he is handsome and always eats sweet food.
He who possesses such steadfast qualities is formidable, yet his origin lies in that which sustains all.
(vi)rodhinī— The rogue has gone abroad to distant lands, and thus the happiness of the family has diminished.
A man born in a year characterized by conflict will have his mental faculties dissolved along with the common folk. || 1 ||
(In the case of a deformity: One who is destitute indeed becomes fierce, possesses long joints, and is filled with great pride.
Even though devoid of beautiful intellect, this youth, the son of an enemy, was born in the year Vikṛti. || 1 ||
(Khara)— Afflicted by lust, with the luster of his body turned ashen, he spoke words that were harsh, drawn out, and trivial.
Such a man will be afflicted by defilements, devoid of shame and proper conduct, and will live for a long time, reaching the age of eighty years.
In Nandana:
One who constructs ponds, large tanks, houses, and wells, who is pure and constantly delights in the giving of food, shall be virtuous.
A man born in the month of Vaiśākha, filled with joy at the birth of a son who brings delight to playful women, shall fear neither men nor gods. || 1 ||
In victory— [he was] exceedingly steadfast in battle, of excellent character, honored by kings, and the most eminent among eloquent speakers.
In the city named Vijaya, there was indeed a donor who was merciless and a slayer of his enemies; from him was born [the one] called Prasūti. || 1 ||
(Jaye)—
In the context of the scriptures, he is a scholar who dispels the dejection of the wise, honorable, generous, and a destroyer of the pride of his enemies.
In the year of Jaya, a man of great power is born who desires victory and is devoted to the objects of the senses.
In the matter of love— he is adorned with ornaments, devoted to the amorous play of women, and skilled in the arts of nectar-like speech.
And one who was born in the year of Manmatha is devoted to fine song and dance and is an enjoyer [of pleasures]. || 1 ||

One born in the year named Durmukhi will have a cruel, arrogant, censurable, and greedy disposition; his face, arms, feet, and teeth will be reddish-brown; he will be fond of opposition, speak contrary words, and engage in many wicked deeds. (1)
(Hemalambini)—
One who possesses horses, golden garments, grain, and jewels, and is exceedingly endowed with sons and daughters.
May that Supreme Person, the source of all, be my refuge—he who is the singular consciousness that grasps all objects as one, like gold suspended [in a crucible]. || 1 ||
One who is procrastinating,
deceitful, excessively greedy, fallen into negligence, blinded by phlegm, and devoid of spiritual essence.
One who speaks excessively regarding undertakings already begun will experience a year of calamities. || 1 ||
(Vikāriṇī):
He is stubborn, proficient in all arts, a clever deceiver, fickle-minded, and a rogue.
One who is not given to much talk, who is free from the conceptualization of a dear friend, and who is subject to change, would be a human being born in the Saṃvatsara year. || 1 ||
In the Śārvaryāṃ [division],
one skilled in the arts of trade, playful, and not at all favorable toward friends.
Devoted to the practice of many sciences, he was born in the year named Śārvari. || 1 ||
139) (In the Plava year)— one who possesses wealth according to his desires, who is constantly satisfied by the purpose of a heart generous through service and respect.
One born in the sign of Aquarius (Plava) will have a well-guarded intellect but a fickle nature. || 1 ||
(Śubhakṛti)—
endowed with good fortune, knowledge, and discipline, he shall also live a long life through incalculable merits.
There may be a human son born of his wife during the Śubhakṛt days, endowed with great wealth. || 1 ||
(Regarding Śobhakṛti): One who is preeminent among all, endowed with the arising of beautiful qualities, a performer of virtuous deeds, and especially victorious.
A husband who is disciplined, virtuous, and highly skilled will bring prosperity and be a source of beauty for one born in the Vatsa year.
(Kraudhinī)— With cruel eyes and an even more cruel nature, he is fond of women and possesses a pride as great as a mountain.
There may be an obstacle at the time of another's undertaking; one becomes angry, and the autumn of anger will be abundant.
(Viśvāvasu:)—
A man with virtuous sons and wife, exceedingly noble, ever devoted to good conduct, and profoundly wise.
One who eats desired food and is delightful with all virtues would have Viśvāvasu as his progeny.
In the event of defeat, he will possess extremely harsh speech and will not properly accumulate any wealth or grain whatsoever.
One who is characterized by conduct that is deficient and deceitful will experience defeat as its result. || 1 ||
(Plavaṅga:)—
One whose mental disposition is always fickle will surely not engage in virtuous deeds.
He was a rogue, devoid of good conduct and reflection; he was a monkey among men, with emaciated limbs. || 1 ||
(Kīlake)—He is to be churned by means of form; he is pleasant-spoken, compassionate, and desires water at every moment.
In the year Kilaka, he was born with thick legs, a noble head, and exceedingly long arms, yet marked by a pockmark.
(If the Moon is strong: Indeed, he shall be learned, wealthy, a possessor of many enjoyments, devoted to deities and guests, and pure.
But the man born in the year Saumya is of a sattvic nature, possessing a slender and delicate body. || 1 ||
(In the common version)— Moving here and there, responsive, skilled in the art of writing, and discerning.
For a living being born of common origin is described as prone to anger, impure, and with a mind withdrawn from enjoyments. || 1 ||
(Virodhikṛti) —
He should be intent on the propitiation of Maheśvara, yet constantly angry and antagonistic toward many.
For he whose very name causes extreme opposition even to his father’s words, turns his face away [from them].
(Running about)— He is learned, of virtuous character, proficient in the arts, wise, and honored by the lords of the earth.
A person indeed becomes one who has attained great status through activity in that which is called "the wandering one. || 1 ||
(To the negligent one: "He is possessed by wicked pride, addicted to quarreling, greedy, devoted to his family, and wretched."
There may be a person of little intelligence who performs censurable deeds, a heedless human being, prone to negligence. (1)
(Ānanda)—
He may be one who gives abundant gifts, clever, exceedingly skillful, and constantly filled with the weight of joy for his sons.
A man who is wise, grateful, exceedingly humble, filled with joy, and generous—[he is truly blessed]. || 1 ||
(Rakṣasa:
He may be one whose deeds are cruel, addicted to quarreling, and who has abandoned the essence of virtuous action and discernment.
A man born in the year of Rākṣasa will be devoid of compassion and even prone to rashness.
(Nala)—
He is possessed of great wisdom, skilled in the prosperity of water-crops and in following the duties of a Vaiśya, and is of excellent character.
One born in the year of Jupiter (Jupiter's year) may have little wealth yet be a protector of many, and such a person is fickle-minded. || 1 ||
In the Piṅgalā [breath]:
one who has reddish-brown eyes and performs censurable deeds is one whose prosperity is fickle and who remains restless.
A man named Piṅgala was born, who was a renouncer, utterly harsh in speech, and extremely cruel. || 1 ||
(Endowed with the right time)—
one who is not given to excessive talk, who has become beloved, who possesses virtuous intelligence, and who is not separated from the prescribed rule.
The association with poets is indeed like Time itself; its application is the power of Time, and its source is the emaciated body.
(Siddhārthinī)— One who has attained fame on the courtyard of the heart, which shines with the radiance of noble intentions, shall be happy.
The minister of the lord of men, having achieved his purpose and being highly honored, becomes a capable man who has attained success. || 1 ||
(Raudra:
Terrifying protector of the sacrificial animals, ever-fond of meat, and a most cunning rogue.
His reputation was ruined, his mental disposition was that of a wicked man, he was exceedingly fierce, and this cruel man was born from a cruel lineage.
One who possesses great pride in the consistency of his own words may, through the force of circumstances, become a person of even lower character.
O you of evil intellect, he who is born in the year of Durmati is a lustful man who, being excessively desirous, is intent upon sin. || 1 ||
(Regarding the Dundubhi drum: One shall always possess the affection and honor of the king, and be endowed with elephants, horses, land, and gold.
If a person born in the Dundubhi year should become exceedingly fond of the delight of the triple symphony (song, dance, and instrumental music), [he will suffer]. || 1 ||
(Rudhirodgāriṇī)—With blood-red eyes, the internal wrath of women toward even a great lover becomes exceedingly emaciated in body due to his sudden appearance.

If [the mark] occurs on both feet, one becomes a person with deformed nails; or else, due to a wound from a weapon on the hand, one undergoes suffering and is born as a non-human being who vomits blood. || 1 ||
O Raktākṣiṇī, a man who is exceedingly devoted to the dharma of right conduct shall become more beautiful than even the god of love himself.
He possesses authority over others, is endowed with some degree of patience, and is afflicted by pain in his eyes and testicles. || 1 ||
In the case of anger—
there would indeed be an obstacle, for it is terrifying due to the excess of the quality of darkness (tamas) in the body of another.
He who was born in the year named Krodhana will strike down the intellect of others at his pleasure. || 1 ||
(At Akṣaya)—
One who utterly squanders the wealth he has acquired, devoted to service, and of cruel disposition.
The activity of one whose mind is small, thinking "the effect exists [in the cause]," indeed results in rebirth when that activity is said to be exhausted. || 1 || 60 ||
Now, the names of the sixty-year cycle beginning with Prabhava—(from the *Daivajñavilāsa*):
Prabhava, Vibhava, Śukla, Pramoda, and Prajāpati.
Āṅgīrasa, Śrīmukha, Bhāva, and Yuvavatsara. || 1 ||
Dhātṛ, Īśvara, Bahudhānya, Pramāthin, Vikrama, and Vṛṣa.
Citrabhānu, Svabhānu, Tāraṇa, Pārthiva, and Vyaya. || 2 ||
Sarvajit, Sarvadhārī, Virodhin, Vikṛti, and Khara.
Nandana, Vijaya, Jaya, Manmatha, and Durmukha. || 3 ||
Hemalambī, Vimalambī, Vikārī, and Śārvarīplava;
Śubhakṛt, Śobhakṛt, Krodhī, Viśvāvasu, and Parābhava. || 4 ||
Plavaṅga, Kīlaka, Saumya, Sādhāraṇa, and Virodhikṛt.
Paridhāvī was Pramādin, and the Rākṣasa Ānanda was Nala. || 5 ||
Piṅgala, Kālayukti, Siddhārthī, Aurodri, and Durmati.
Duṇḍubhī, Rudhirōdgārī, Raktākṣī, Krodhanā, and Akṣayā. || 6 ||
These sixty years, beginning with Prabhava, are to be known by the wise as the names of the years.
Now, the names of the presiding deities of the sixty-year cycle beginning with Prabhava (according to the Śaiva Āgama):
Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Maheśa, Gaṇeśa, and likewise Gaṇapa.
Ṣaḍānana, Vallī, Gaurī, Brahmī, and Maheśvarī. || 1 ||
Kaumārī, Vaiṣṇavī, as well as Vārāhī and Aindrī.
Cāmuṇḍika, Aroga, Bhrāja, and Paṭara as well. || 2 ||
Pataṅga, Svarṇarocis, Jyotiṣmat, Vibhāsa, and Kaśyapa.
Ravi, Sūrya, Bhānu, Khaga, and likewise Pūṣan. || 3 ||
Hiraṇyagarbha, Atharvan, Marīci, Āditya, and likewise Savitṛ;
Then there are Arka, Bhāskara, Agni, Jātavedas, and Sahaujas. || 4 ||
Then Jarāprabhu, Vaiśvānara, and Naryāpasa as well—
And Paṅktiratha, Visarpi, as well as Matsya, Kūrma, and Varāha. || 5 ||
Narasimha, Vamana, Sri Rama, Bhargava, and Halin;
Kṛṣṇa, Kalkī, Buddhadurga, Dhāna, and Bhairava. || 6 ||
Hanumān, Śāradā, Ākṣāyaṇī, and Lakṣmī are thus remembered.
The presiding deities of these years follow in sequence according to their prideful conceits.
Now, the forms of the presiding deities of the sixty-year cycle beginning with Prabhava (according to the Śaiva Āgama):
93. First, the meditation on Brahmā, the presiding deity of Prabhava:

He has four faces, his lotus-hands are marked with the *akṣasūtra* and other signs; he holds the gesture of fearlessness (*abhaya*) and the *cinmudrā* in his two hands, and he stands upon a fully blossomed lotus seat.
I worship the lotus-born one named Prabhava, who bestows the increase of prosperity, and whose chest shines with the brilliant *brahmasūtra* (sacred thread) that radiates pure splendor. (1)
The color of a lotus. || 1 ||

94. Now, the meditation on the deity Viṣṇu, who possesses the conceit of non-existence (*vibhava*): [He is] resplendent with a crown, and delightful with the discus, the Śārṅga bow, and the mace, accompanied by four [attendants].
One should meditate upon the Lord of the gods, the sovereign of all power, seated upon the Ananta throne with his hands [in the appropriate mudrās]. || 1 ||
He is cloud-dark in complexion. || 1 ||
95. Now, the meditation on Maheśvara as the presiding deity of Śukla:
[He is] with matted hair, his limbs adorned with ornaments of serpents, three-eyed, with the moon upon the edge of his crown, and wearing a tiger skin as an upper garment.
I bow to Girīśa, who is known as Śukla, whose vehicle is the excellent bull, who is saluted by the lords of gods and sages, and who holds a trident in his hand. || 1 ||
White in color. || 1 ||
96. Now, the meditation on Gaṇeśa as Pramodūtābhimānin:
[He who has] the auspicious face of the lord of elephants, radiant with a single tusk, and is named Pramodūtākṛta.
One should constantly meditate upon Gaṇeśa, seated upon a mouse, who bestows the pacification of obstacles, within the lotus of the heart. || 1 ||
He is red in color. || 1 ||
97. Now, the meditation on Gaṇapati, the presiding power over Prajāpati and the year:
[I meditate upon her] who holds a beautiful spear with a face like that of the lord of elephants, who has four arms, and who is adorned with a digit of the moon.
I bow to her who is the full moon for the ocean of the devotees' desires, and whose name is Prajotpattikṛt (the Creator of Progeny). || 1 ||
She is red in color. || 1 ||
98. Now, the meditation on Ṣaṇmukha, who takes pride in being a descendant of Aṅgiras:
[He has] a single arm blazing with power, wears a crown of the moon, and is mounted upon a peacock.
We praise the six-faced one named Āṅgirasa, the commander-in-chief of Indra’s army.
He is red in color. || 1 ||
99. Now, the meditation on the deity Vallī of Śrīmukhābhimānin:
She has a moon-like face and beautiful eyes, rides upon a cock, and is constantly held within the cave [of the heart].
I meditate upon the creeper named Śrīmukhā, which bestows the increase of spiritual welfare. || 1 ||
The color of the Pāṭala flower. || 1 ||

100. Now, the visualization of the deity Gaurī, who possesses the conceit of being a living being: One should meditate on Gaurī, the daughter of the Lord of Mountains, seated upon an excellent bull, bearing a digit of the moon.
I praise Mahāmīḍā, who is called Bhāvā, the full moon at the end of the ocean of the curiosity of worldly existence. || 1 ||
She is the color of emerald. || 1 ||
101. Now follows the meditation on the Brahmī deity associated with youth:
I praise that goddess known as Youth (Yuvā), the Brāhmī whose feet are saluted by Brahmā and the other gods.
Mounted upon a preeminent swan, she possesses a beauty and charm that captivate the heart of Śambhu. || 1 ||
Golden-hued. || 1 ||
102. Now, the meditation on Māheśvarī, who takes pride in the elements:
May she, known as the element, shine eternally within the heart-lotus of Māheśvarī.
Adorned with the moon as her crest-jewel, she is the constant bestower of prosperity and growth upon Śambhu.
She is of radiant white complexion. || 1 ||
103. Now, the meditation on Kaumārī, who is identified with Īśvara:
I praise Kaumārī, the bestower of prosperity, who is forever mounted upon a peacock.
That portion designated as Īśvara, which by its very nature bestows satisfaction to the hands [of the practitioner]. || 1 ||
The color of the Pāṭala flower. || 1 ||
104. Now, the meditation on Vaiṣṇavī as Bahudhānyā:
I constantly meditate upon the goddess Vaiṣṇavī, known by the name Bahudhānyā, within my heart.
I perpetually bow to her who dwells on the left lap of Śaṅkara and bestows desired objects.
Her complexion is dark like a cloud. || 1 ||
105. Now, the meditation on Vārāhī, who possesses the conceit of the Destroyer: I bow to Vārāhī, who is like the full moon to the ocean of joy of Śiva.
She who bestows the increase of the highest good and has assumed her own name, "Pramāthī. ||1||
She is dark-complexioned. || 1 ||
106. Now, the meditation on Indrāṇī, who possesses the pride of valor:
We contemplate Māhendrī, known by the name Vikramā, seated upon a bull-throne.
For the sake of peace, [I worship] her who wears a radiant moon as a crown, who grants the desires of her devotees, and who is the dispeller of fear. || 1 ||
Golden-colored. || 1 ||
107. Now, the meditation on Cāmuṇḍā, who presides over the year of the equinox (viṣuvat): I here salute Cāmuṇḍā, whose limbs are beautiful, and who is seated upon a bull-throne.
She who is named Viṭṛṣu, who is worthy of worship by the gods, and who incessantly brings about the destruction of the race of the Daityas. || 1 ||
Black in color. || 1 ||
108. Now, the meditation on the presiding deity of the year Citrabhānu, who is the god of freedom from disease: I praise the one called Aroga, Citrabhānu, for constant joy.
Mounted upon an excellent horse, his head radiant with a crown. || 1 ||
Red in color. || 1 ||
109. Now, the meditation on the radiant deity presiding over the year Svabhānu: One should meditate upon the one named Bhrāja, who is Svabhānu, the bestower of health and accomplishment upon men.
I bow to him who is mounted upon an elephant, with a shining sword and shield in his hands. || 1 ||
He is red in color. || 1 ||
110. Now, the meditation on the deity of the *paṭara* who possesses the conceit of being the Savior (*tāraṇa*):
I constantly contemplate the one called *paṭara* within the lotus of my inner heart.
The crossing over, the journey of the sun, and the lotus-hand that illuminates the trident. || 1 ||
Red in color. || 1 ||
111. Now, the meditation on the deity Pataṅga, who possesses the pride of being the year of the earth (Pārthiva): "I take refuge in Pataṅga, who is called Pārthiva and is mounted upon a bull."
I worship the divine one who bears the conch and the discus and wears yellow garments. || 1 ||
Red in color. || 1 ||
112. Now, the meditation on the deity of Vyaya, known as Svarṇara:
I take refuge in the one named Vyaya, who is mounted upon a golden cuckoo.
He who has the moon as his crest-ornament, matted hair, three eyes, and shines with a trident.
Red in color. || 1 ||
113. Now, the meditation on the deity Jyotiṣmat, who presides over the year Sarvajit:
I praise the one named Sarvajit, the radiant Jyotiṣmat, the bestower of blessings.
He has a *bhṛśuṇḍī* weapon and a noose in his lotus-like hands, is mounted upon a tiger, and possesses three eyes. || 1 ||
Red in color. || 1 ||
114. Now, the meditation on the deity Vibhāsa, who possesses the conceit of being the Sustainer of All:
[One should meditate upon] the Sun named Vibhāsa, who is called the Sustainer of All.
For the attainment of desired goals, I always bow to Him who is seated upon a chariot drawn by seven horses.
He is red in color. (The remainder is like that of Sūrya; Ni0 5) || 1 ||
115. Now, the meditation on the deity Kaśyapa, who presides over the Virodhin year:
One should meditate upon him, seated on a throne of Meru’s peak, known by the name Virodhin.
I bow to Kaśyapa, who has five faces and ten arms. || 1 ||
He is red in color. (The remainder is like that of the Sun; Ni0 5) || 1 ||
116. Now, the meditation on the Sun-god, who is the presiding deity of Vikṛti: I worship the Sun, named Vikṛti, who has three heads and six arms.
Mounted upon the lord of serpents and clothed in beautiful yellow garments.
He is red in color. (The remainder is like that of the Sun; Ni0 5) || 1 ||
117. Now, the meditation on the deity Sūrya, who possesses the conceit of being harsh: Mounted upon the best of birds, clothed in blue garments.
I salute the one named Sūrya, who has four faces and eight arms. || 1 ||
He is red in color. (The remainder is like that of Sūrya; Ni0 5) || 1 ||
118. Now follows the meditation on the deity Bhānu, who possesses the pride of being Nandana:
[One should meditate upon] Bhānu, named Nandana, beautifully adorned with splendor.
I worship the one who has the lord of beasts as his vehicle, who possesses five faces and ten arms. || 1 ||
He is red in color. (The remainder is like that of Sūrya; Ni0 5) || 1 ||
119. Now, the visualization of the bird-deity Vijayābhimāninī: [He is] six-faced, twelve-armed, and seated upon a tiger-vehicle.
I salute the one named Vijaya, who wears a tiger-skin garment. || 1 ||
He is red in color. (The remainder is like that of the Sun; Ni0 5) || 1 ||
120. Now, the meditation on the deity Pūṣan, who possesses the pride of victory:
[one should meditate upon] Pūṣan, named Jaya, the bestower of boons upon the multitude of his devotees.
I take refuge in the heart of him whose pair of hands are marked with the conch and the discus. || 1 ||
Red in color. || 1 ||
121. Now, the meditation on the deity Hiraṇyagarbha, who identifies with Manmatha:
[One should meditate on him] as mounted upon an excellent swan, with his hand adorned by a lute.
I bow to Hiraṇyagarbha, whose body is named Manmatha, the bestower of my desires. || 1 ||
He is red in color. || 1 ||

122. Now, the meditation on the deity Marīci, who is Durmukha by name and possesses the pride [of that form]: one should meditate on Marīci, known as Durmukha, mounted upon a monkey of wrathful aspect.
With joy, I take refuge in him whose mouth is wide open, bestowing fear upon the world. || 1 ||
He is red in color. (The rest is like the Sun; Ni0 5) || 1 ||
123. Now, the meditation on the deity Āditya, who possesses the conceit of being Hemalaṃba: Āditya is the abode of splendor, known by the name Hemalambi.
I take refuge in the Eye of the worlds, mounted upon the seven-horsed chariot. || 1 ||
He is red in color. (The remainder is like that of the Sun; Ni0 5) || 1 ||
124. Now, the meditation on the deity Savitṛ, who is the conceited Vimālambin: "With my mind, I remember the Sun-god known as Vimālambi."
Holding a bow and arrows in his two arms, he has an excellent horse as his vehicle.
He is red in color. || 1 ||
125. Now, the meditation on the deity Arka, who identifies with the object of transformation (*vikārya*): [One should meditate on] Arka, named Vikārin, who is harsh and whose weapon is a saw.
I bow to the One-Eyed One, mounted upon a fierce tiger. || 1 ||
Red in color. || 1 ||
126. Now, the meditation on the deity Bhāskara, who presides over the night: [One should meditate on] Bhāskara, known as Śārvarī, whose radiance fills the quarters of the horizon.
I bow to the one whose hands are radiant with the discus, who is seated upon a shining chariot. || 1 ||
Red in color. || 1 ||
127. Now, the meditation on the deity Agni, who is identified with the raft:
I bow to Agni, who possesses a garland of widespread flames and dispels darkness.
Mounted upon a goat, with four arms and two heads, he is known as Plava. || 1 ||
He is red in color. (The remainder is as for Agni; Ni0 4) || 1 ||
128. Now, the meditation on the deity Jātavedas, who possesses the conceit of being the "Doer of Good" (Śubhakṛt):
"I always praise Jātavedas, whose name is Śubhakṛt."
Seated upon a swing, he is auspicious, bearing a sword and a shield. || 1 ||
Red in color. || 1 ||
129. Now, the meditation on the deity Sahojas-Śobhakṛt:
I take refuge in Sahojas-Śobhakṛt, who bestows the desired objects upon men.
Mounted upon the palanquin-bearer, with two chowries in his hands. || 1 ||
Red in color. || 1 ||
130. Now, the meditation on the deity Krodhyabhimānyajarāprabhu:
"I praise the Lord Ajara-prabhu, who has the name 'Krodhin' (the Wrathful One)."
He was constantly mounted upon a chariot drawn by oxen, with his lotus-like hand radiant with a spear.
Red in color. || 1 ||
131. Now, the meditation on the deity Vaiśvānara, who presides over the Viśvāvasu year:
"I constantly worship Vaiśvānara, who is invoked by the name Viśvāvasu."
He was mounted upon a man-vehicle (naravāhana), bearing a sword and a shield, and was auspicious.
Red in color. || 1 ||
132. Now, the meditation on the deity Naryāpasa, known as Parābhava: I praise the one named Parābhava, the Naryāpasa who blazes with great luster.
Mounted upon a lofty horse, with a battle-axe held resplendent in his hand. || 1 ||
Red in color. || 1 ||
133. Now follows the meditation on the deity Paṅtirādha, who identifies with the monkey (plavaṃga):
"One should praise Agni as Paṅtirādha, who is well-known as Plavaṃga."
He is always mounted upon his excellent white horse and holds the Śārṅga bow and arrows.
He is red in color. || 1 ||
134. Now, the visualization of the deity presiding over the Kīlaka:
I take refuge in the spreading fire known as Kīlaka.
Mounted upon a lofty elephant, with his lotus-like hand radiant with a trident. || 1 ||
Red in color. || 1 ||
135. Now, the meditation on the deity of the Fish, who possesses a gentle nature: I bow my head to Hari in the form of the Fish, known as Saumya.
His hands are radiant with the conch and the discus, and he is the bestower of the desires of his devotees.
White in color. || 1 ||
136. Now, the meditation on the common presiding deity Kūrma: I salute the one in the form of a tortoise, the sustainer of Mount Mandara.
He held the Kaumodakī club and the Śārṅga bow in his hands, and he was addressed by the common name [Kṛṣṇa].
Golden-colored. || 1 ||

137. Now, the meditation on the deity Varāha, the presiding lord of the year Virodhikṛt: one should meditate upon Hari, who has assumed the form of a boar and upon whose tusk rests a portion of the earth.
I salute the one who grants boons and fearlessness, who is heard of as the "Virodhikṛt. || 1 ||
He is dark-complexioned. || 1 ||
138. Now, the meditation on the deity Nṛsiṃha, who presides over the *parīdhāvya* verses: I worship that Hari, whose body is that of a man-lion, the tearer of the pillar.
I invoke Parīdhāvikṛta, the bestower of joy upon Prahlāda. || 1 ||
White in color. || 1 ||
139. Now, the meditation on the deity Vāmana for those who are negligent and conceited:
I worship Hari in the form of Vāmana, whose hand holds a resplendent umbrella.
It causes the torment of the offering and is called "the one made by negligence."
He is dark-complexioned, like the blade of dūrvā grass. || 1 ||
140. Now, the meditation on the deity Śrī Rāma, who identifies with Ānanda:
I take refuge in the beloved of Sītā, the generator of joy for the entire world.
To him named Rāmamānanda, who held a bow and arrows.
He is dark-complexioned. || 1 ||
141. Now, the visualization of the deity Śrī Paraśurāma, who possesses the pride of a Rākṣasa:
[He is] adorned with a mass of matted hair, his hand blazing with an axe.
I pray that Bhārgava Rāma may truly destroy the one called Rākṣasa. || 1 ||
Golden-colored. || 1 ||
142. Now, the visualization of the deity Balarāma, who takes pride in Nala:
[He whose] lotus-hand illuminates the plow, and who is clothed in blue garments.
I salute Balarāma and the one named Nala day and night. || 1 ||
Of bright complexion. || 1 ||
143. Now, the meditation on the deity Kṛṣṇa, who possesses the conceit of being Piṅgala:
[one should meditate upon] Kṛṣṇa, named Piṅgala, whose form is radiant with the plumage of a peacock.
I take refuge in that dance, whose hands are radiant like fresh butter, within my heart. || 1 ||
He is dark-complexioned. || 1 ||
144. Now, the visualization of the deity Kalki, who is characterized by the timing [of his appearance] and possesses conceit regarding that timing:
he bears hatred toward the rows of barbarians and is named for his connection with the timing of the end of the age.
He is always mounted upon a white bull, with bow and arrow in hand.
White in color. || 1 ||
145. Now, the meditation on the Buddha-deity named Siddhārthika: I worship him who bears the name Siddhārthika and possesses the form of a Buddha.
Naked, with a deformed body, he was the cause of the assault upon the woman.
The color of the *pāṭala* flower. || 1 ||
146. Now, the visualization of the deity Durgā, who presides over the year Raudri:
[one should meditate on] Durgā, known by the name Raudrikṛtā, for the removal of calamities.
I meditated upon that slayer of Daityas, who was intent on tasting blood.
Blue in color. || 1 ||
147. Now, the visualization of the deity Yātudhāna, who possesses the conceit of evil intellect:
[one should visualize] Yātudhāna as having a wide mouth, a single eye, and a fierce appearance.
I meditate upon that which is called Durmatītikṛt for the sake of pacifying undesirable things.
Blue in color. || 1 ||
148. Now, the visualization of the deity Bhairava, who presides over the drum (dundubhi):
He who causes the drum to sound its call and strikes terror into all enemies.
And I take refuge in Bhairava, who is mounted upon his excellent vehicle and is clothed only by the directions.
He is dark-complexioned. || 1 ||

149. Now, the visualization of the deity Hanumān, the slayer of Abhimāna, who is born of blood and the son of Vāyu: [one should meditate upon] Hanumān, the son of Vāyu, known by the name Rudhirodgārin.
I take refuge in the one with the long tail who is intent on leaping across the ocean. || 1 ||
Golden-hued. || 1 ||
150. Now, the meditation on the deity Sarasvatī who identifies with Raktākṣī: One should meditate upon the radiant Sarasvatī, whose lotus-like hands shine with a lute.
I take refuge in the goddess named Raktākṣī, who bestows the power of speech.
White in color. || 1 ||
151. Now, the meditation on the deity Krodhanābhimānidākṣāyaṇī:
[One should meditate upon] Dākṣāyaṇī, known as Krodhanā, the destroyer of Dakṣa’s sacrifice.
One should worship her, who is mounted upon a parrot and holds a trident, for the attainment of one's desired goals. || 1 ||
Golden-hued. || 1 ||
152. Now, the visualization of the deity Lakṣmī, whose nature is the conceit of inexhaustibility: I take refuge in that Lakṣmī, known as the Inexhaustible, the daughter of the Ocean of Milk.
She is mounted upon a swan, moon-faced, with her two hands forming lotuses.
Golden-colored. || 1 || 60 ||
153. Now, the nature of the southern course (dakṣiṇāyana)—according to the Śaiva Āgama:
"That which is indeed known as the southern course is dark-complexioned and has eyes like those of the moon."
Wearing yellow garments and carrying a water-pot, he had the appearance of a *karṇikāra* petal. || 1 ||
The seed, the sprout, the bowl, the sun, and the hand of man—these [are the factors] that act incessantly.
When worshipped constantly, he leads to success and the abundance of wealth and grain.
He is dark-complexioned. || 1 ||
154. Now, the nature of the northern course (uttarāyaṇa)—(in the Śaiva Āgama): This one known as the northern course is white in color and large-eyed.
Clad in madder-dyed garments and adorned with ornaments of gold and pearls.
A book in the right hand and the orb of the sun in the left.
One should offer curd for the sake of liberation and joy, but it should be worshipped for the sake of fame.
White in color. || 1 || 2 ||

155. Now, the definition of the solstice (*ayana*): (In Bhaṭṭabhāskara’s *Ratnamālā*)—the three seasons beginning with Śiśira are indeed the northern solstice (*uttarāyaṇa*), and during that time, the day is said to be divine.
The other three seasons are said to be the night of the gods, and that [night] is also the day of the Maruts. || 1 || 2 ||
Now, Satyavrata states the application of these two [solstices] in the Mādhavīya:
"The consecration of deities, groves, tanks, and so forth, should take place when the sun faces the north."
One who performs it facing the southern direction shall not obtain its fruit. || 1 ||
150) (In the Vaikhānasa-saṃhitā:
Mātṛ-bhairava, Vārāha, Narasiṃha, and Trivikrama.
And the slayer of the demon Mahiṣāsura should indeed be installed during the southern transit of the sun (dakṣiṇāyana).
In the *Madanaratnajyotiḥśāstra*:
house-entry, the consecration of deities, marriage, the tonsure ceremony (*caula*), and the investiture of the sacred thread (*vratabandha*) [are described] first.
Auspicious rites are prescribed for the northern course [of the sun], while those that are censured indeed pertain to the southern course. (1)
Now, the specific acts of giving to be performed during the two solstices— (from the *Dānacintāmaṇi*): therein, the gifts during the northern solstice—
(from the *Skanda Purāṇa*)—
O King, he who gives a cow made of sesame seeds during the northern course of the sun [attains great merit].
One attains all desires and finds supreme bliss. || 1 ||
(In the Viṣṇudharmottara):
O Brahmins, the gift of clothing during the northern transit of the sun yields great fruit.
By giving a bull filled with sesame seeds, one is liberated from diseases.
Now, regarding the rites of giving during the southern solstice—(in the Bhaviṣyottara Purāṇa):
"During the southern solstice, one should worship the Lord with rice grains mixed with sesame seeds."
Or one may perform the consecration with clarified butter, desiring the fruit of great merit. || 1 ||
With a vessel full of ghee that has a hole, day and night.
Or with cow-derived clarified butter, one should offer a "butter-blanket" (ghṛtakambala) to Śambhu.
Having fashioned a beautiful image out of clarified butter for the sake of increasing one's welfare.

Now, the qualities of one born during the two solstices (*ayanau*), according to the *Jātakābharaṇa*: One who is born during the two solstices is perpetually cheerful, has a wife who is not prone to jealousy, is endowed with extreme contentment, and possesses a very long life.
He is a giver of protection to men, noble, yet fearful; his birth is from one born of a gentle lineage.
He has no regard for his own labor, yet performs the work of agriculture; he possesses a heart exceedingly cruel toward four-footed creatures.
Though deceitful and intolerant, he who possessed inferential knowledge reached the distance of a yojana during the southern solstice.
156. Now, the nature of the solar deity presiding over the southern solstice (*dakṣiṇāyana*)—(according to the Śaiva Āgama):
"For the sake of ever-increasing welfare, I eternally take refuge in the southern solstice."
The Sun, mounted upon his radiant chariot, surrounded by the moon and the stars.
Red in color. || 1 ||
157. Now, the nature of the deity Soma, who presides over the northern solstice—(in the Śaiva Āgama):
"I constantly take refuge in the northern solstice for the removal of afflictions."
Mounted upon a divine chariot, accompanied by the sun and other celestial bodies.
White in color. || 1 ||
151) Now, the essential natures of the seasons—(according to the Śaivāgama and the Nṛsiṃhaprāsāda)—158. Among these, first is the essential nature of the spring season:
I praise the primordial Spring, who is seated upon a tiger skin.
With hands raised holding a rosary, he was devoted to the five-syllable mantra.
The glorious Spring, covered by a canopy of flowers, is the bestower of desired objects.
Seated in the bound lotus posture (baddhapadmāsana), facing east with a smiling countenance. || 2 ||
He was white-bodied with red eyes, and was clothed in yellow garments.
With all his limbs smeared with ashes, he dwells here in joy and delight. || 1 ||
White in color. || 1 ||
159. Now, the nature of the summer season:
The second, named Summer, has dusty and coarse limbs.
His hand holds a rosary and the sun, and he is endowed with a moon-white parasol.
He should be worshipped by the wise for the destruction of the torment of disease.
In the summer, he sat facing the east upon a seat honored by sages.
I bow my head daily to him whose hand is radiant with a water-pot (kamaṇḍalu). || 1 ||
Smoke-colored. || 1 ||
160. Now, the nature of the rainy season:
The third season, that of the clouds, is green in color and has large, reddish-brown eyes.
He was accompanied by a copper-colored parrot and wore earrings of blue coral.
Holding a jar filled with water against his chest, he bears the sign of the fish.
He was indeed enveloped by a mass of clouds, possessed of lightning, and radiant with light.
He should be worshipped with plates of yellow orpiment for the sake of increasing nourishment and contentment.
Today, with my head bowed, I prostrate myself before those who proclaim the joy of the rainy season.
Constantly seated upon grass mats, they remained facing the south.
He is yellowish-green in color. || 1 ||
161. Now, the nature of the autumn season:
The fourth season is autumn; its deity is white as the moon and possesses beautiful eyes.
A string of pearls upon his neck, and emerald earrings in his ears.
He should place the lunar disc on the right eye and a jar filled with nectar on the left.
Wearing this [garland], which is worthy of worship, leads to the increase of longevity and happiness. || 2 ||
For this autumn will indeed be the bestower of the objects we have prayed for.
The season, seated facing westward, wears a crystal bracelet.
The color of the moon and white. || 4 ||
162. Now, the nature of the winter season (hemanta): Winter is to be known as the fifth [season], tawny-colored, and adorned with horns and earrings.
Clad in yellow garments, with three matted locks of hair, and wearing a black antelope skin; || 1 ||
In the southwest (dakṣiṇa) is Dhānyamañjarī; on the left is a vessel containing coriander (dhānyaka).
He is to be worshipped for the sake of prosperity and for the increase of the abundance of grain. || 2 ||
The winter season has taken its place for us, facing the north.
Pure and wearing the sacred thread, may he who bestows auspiciousness be gracious. || 1 ||
He is of a tawny color. || 1 ||
163. Now, the nature of the winter season (śiśira):
The sixth, known as Śiśira, has eyes that are reddish at the corners like a green leaf.
With golden earrings upon his ears and a necklace of coral upon his neck.
The Madhūka flower is the mark upon it; the vessel is the lotus of the sun’s rays.
And one who holds a vessel of unhusked rice for the sake of increasing prosperity. || 2 ||
I bow my head to Śiśira, the season standing at the zenith.
Holding a sun-disc in his hand, he was intent on the recitation of the five-syllable mantra. || 1 ||
The color is yellow. || 1 || 6 ||
(Regarding the description of the six seasons here, this is the concluding verse illustrating their respective natures—[from] the *Śāntiprakaraṇa* of the *Śaivāgama*): || - ||
And the specific characteristics of each respective image as stated in the final verses of those various chapters.
(In the *Nṛsiṃhaprāsāda*):

Thus, because there is a difference in the essential form of the image due to differences in opinion, both [views] are mentioned with the intention that the image should be fashioned according to whichever one pleases the devotee.
Now, the gifts to be performed during the seasons such as spring—(from the *Dānacintāmaṇi*, based on the *Viṣṇudharmottara*).
The giving of baths, ointments, and so forth is prescribed for the spring season.
Likewise, [there were] vehicles in the intense heat, and immediately after that, umbrellas. || 1 ||
(From the Devīpurāṇa):
Furthermore, O dear one, he who, according to the prescribed rite, [worships] the Goddess during the rainy season...
He bestows sesame seeds and other such items upon brahmins and upon the daughters of brahmins. || 1 ||
He attains satisfaction through that very knowledge very swiftly indeed.
(From the Viṣṇudharmottara):
O knower of dharma, [the gift] of food is [recommended] in autumn, and likewise of garments in winter.
Having performed the gift of fire, a man should dedicate it to the Sun at dawn. || 1 ||
Having likewise constantly gratified the fire with sesame seeds during the cool season, one attains success.
Having given groats mixed with excellent ghee to the twice-born according to one's ability. || 2 ||
One attains the manifestation of a blazing fire from one's body and the destruction of enemies.
Now, the qualities of those born during the seasons beginning with spring (from the *Jātakābharaṇa*): First, regarding spring (*vasanta*)—
one who possesses the form of Kāmadeva, is wise, powerful, and proficient in the science of music and in mathematics.
A person born in the spring season is clear-minded, possessing a mental disposition as pure as the blades and missiles of weapons. || 1 ||
(In summer)—endowed with sovereignty, knowledge, wealth, and grain; a speaker; with long, pure, and curly locks of hair.
One who has undergone birth during the summer season shall become an enjoyer of pleasures and not one inclined toward reflection. || 1 ||
(Regarding the rainy season:
He is courageous in battle, wise, majestic, fond of horses, and handsome.
A man whose nature consists of phlegm and wind, who delights in dalliance with women, and who is joyful throughout the year, is a Vaipuruṣa. || 1 ||
(autumn) —
A person born under [the influence of] Vāyu will have unfulfilled anger, be proud, wealthy, devoted to dharma, and pure.
He who delights in battle, is endowed with vehicles, and whose birth occurs during the season known as autumn. || 1 ||
In Hemanta,
the minister of the king shall be a man who is clever, very generous, and endowed with charming virtues.
Devoted to the dharma of virtuous deeds, wise, born in the winter season, and ever humble. || 1 ||
In the cold season, he is fond of refined food and drink, disciplined, dear to his teachers, and gentle toward his sons and wife.
A person who is dressed for virtuous deeds, yet is wrathful and endowed with strength, was born in the season of Śiśira (winter). || 1 || 6 ||
Now, the names of the deities presiding over the six seasons (according to the Śaiva Āgama):
Kāma, Agni, Varuṇa, Gaurī, Sarpa, and Īśvara.
These have been proclaimed as the presiding deities of the six seasons. || 1 ||

Now, the forms of the presiding deities of the six seasons (according to the Śaiva Āgama): 164. First among them is the form of the deity Kāma, who presides over the spring season—the leader of the spring time, the bestower of desired objects.
I worship Him who has pierced the three worlds with his flower-arrows. || 1 ||
Golden-colored. || 1 ||
165. Now, the nature of the deity Agni, who presides over the summer season: [one should worship] the pure Vahni, the leader of summer, situated in Aries, the pervasive one.
The God, beloved by his devotees, is enriched with a spear, a *sruk*, and a *sruva* in his hands.
Red in color. || 1 ||
166. Now, the nature of the deity Varuṇa, who presides over the rainy season:
I salute Pracetas, the presiding deity (adhidaivata) of the rainy season.
Mounted upon a crocodile, holding a noose in his hand, he is the bestower of life to the worlds. || 1 ||
Golden-hued. || 1 ||

167. Now, the nature of the goddess Girijā, who presides over the season of autumn: [I bow to] her who is a portion of Girijā, whose body is half that of Śaṅkara, and who is the presiding deity of the autumnal season.
One should worship the sole mother of the world, the bestower of all desired objects.
She is yellowish-green in color. || 1 ||
168. Now, the nature of the serpent deity presiding over the winter season: the sovereign of the serpent race, the presiding deity of winter.
May this great being, the son of Kadrū, protect us at all times. || 1 ||
White in color. || 1 ||
169. Now, the nature of the deity Maheśa, the Lord who presides over the winter season:
one should worship Maheśa, the Lord of winter, whose banner bears the bull.
I bow to the destroyer of Tripura; may he grant me my desired object. || 1 ||
White in color. || 1 || 6 ||
Now, according to the lunar reckoning, the nature of the months beginning with Caitra—(in the Śaiva Āgama):
First, the nature of the month of Caitra:
[He] whose hands shine with the conch and discus, and whose head is resplendent with a crown.
We worship the month of Madhu, which generates joy for the entire world. || 1 ||
Red in color. || 1 ||
171. Now, the nature of the month of Vaiśākha:
[One should meditate on] the month known as Mādhava, who bears the Kaumodakī mace and the Śārṅga bow.
I salute Him who is mounted upon the vehicle Garuḍa for the attainment of my desired goal. || 1 ||
White in color. || 1 ||
172. Now, the nature of the month of Jyeṣṭha: [He is] the three-eyed, six-armed Brahmā, with the space between his arms radiant with the sacrificial thread.
We worship Śuklamāsa, who is mounted upon a tiger-vehicle. || 1 ||
White in color. || 1 ||
173. Now, the nature of the month of Āṣāḍha:
[He is] two-headed, four-armed, and has the lord of serpents as his vehicle.
We worship the pure month of Mārgaśīrṣa, the bestower of the desires of his devotees. || 1 ||
The color is reddish-brown. || 1 ||
174. Now, the nature of the month of Śrāvaṇa:
I bow to the month of Nabhas today for the removal of all afflictions.
Five-faced and ten-armed, seated upon an excellent deer.
He is yellowish-green in color. || 1 ||
175. Now, the nature of the month of Bhādrapada:
I bow to the month known as Nabhasya for the attainment of my desired goal.
He has four faces and eight arms, and is seated upon an excellent swan. || 1 ||
White in color. || 1 ||
176. Now, the nature of the month of Āśvayuja: [He is] six-faced, twelve-armed, and seated upon an excellent bear.
We constantly worship the Lord who bestows the desired objects of His devotees, the source of nourishment and sustenance. || 1 ||
The color is reddish-orange. || 1 ||
177. Now, the nature of the month of Kārttika:
[One should meditate upon] the three-eyed one, with beautiful matted hair, and adorned with the beautiful crescent moon as his crest-ornament.
We worship the one who has ascended the peak of Kailāsa during the month of Mārgaśīrṣa. || 1 ||
White in color. || 1 ||
178. Now, the nature of the month of Mārgaśīrṣa: [He is] mounted upon a bull, holding a trident in his hand, and attended by beautiful women.
I bow my head in reverence to the God named Sahas, day after day, month after month.
White in color. || 1 ||
179. Now, the nature of the month of Puṣya:
[He is] mounted upon the vehicle of a śārikā bird, with a sword and a shield in his hands.
I shall meditate daily in my mind upon the invincible one for the month of Sahasya.
He is yellowish-green in color. || 1 ||
180. Now, the nature of the month of Māgha:
[He] whose hand is radiant with the moon-like smile, who has the excellent parrot as his vehicle.
With a one-pointed mind, I constantly meditate upon the month of Tapas, which bestows all desired fruits. || 1 ||
He is yellowish-green in color. || 1 ||
181. Now, the nature of the month of Phālguna:
I praise the month of Tapasya, in which the excellent cuckoo resides.
His shoulders were radiant with the sacred thread (brahmasūtra), and his head was adorned with a crown.
The color of the *pāṭala* flower. || 1 || 12 ||
Now, the colors of the months beginning with Caitra—(as stated in the Viṣṇudharmottara and the Kāraṇāgama): Caitra is honey-colored and red; Vaiśākha is Mādhava and white.
Jyeṣṭha is bright white in color, while Śuci and Āṣāḍhaka are reddish. || 1 ||
Śrāvaṇa, however, is green in color, and its deity is remembered as Nabhas.
Bhādrapada and Āśvayuja shall be white; Kārttika shall be ruddy. || 2 ||
