It belongs to the human class (*manuṣyagaṇa*). Its source is the serpent (*bhujaṃga-yoni*). Brahmā is its presiding deity (*devatā*). It is of the Śūdra caste. It is four-footed. Its face is turned upward. It is blind in one eye. It is stable. Its central star is the middle one. Its location is a city (*pattana*). Its mandala is that of Indra. Its tree is the Jambū. Its bird is the cock. Its two syllables are *u* and *ṛ*. In this asterism, Kṛṣṇa and Bhīma were born. After forty *ghaṭikās*, there are four poisonous *nāḍīs*. Eating rice-pudding mixed with ghee during a journey toward the east or north is auspicious. For fever, there is misfortune for seven days. For its pacification, the rite for worshiping the deity Brahmā is as follows: Black cloth; musk scent; white water-lily (*kahlāra*) flower; guggulu incense; an offering of milk-rice (*kṣīrānna*); having worshipped with the sixteen services (*ṣoḍaśopacāra*) using the mantra "Oṃ namo brahmaṇe," one should offer oblations (*homa*) one hundred and eight times with the Gāyatrī mantra using seven types of grains mixed with clarified butter. One should offer a bali-oblation of milk-rice with perfumes and garlands in the eastern direction. In this asterism, a woman experiencing her first menses becomes beloved by her husband and possesses sons. In this asterism, the following auspicious rites are recommended: conception (*ṛtu*), the parting of the hair (*sīmantonnayana*), the male-ascertaining rite (*puṃsavana*), the tonsure (*caula*), the sacred thread ceremony (*upanayana*), the study of the Vedas and Shastras, the return home (*samāvartana*), marriage, oil-massage (*tailābhyaṅga*), wearing ornaments, the coronation of a king, ascending the throne, swinging on a swing, the acquisition of a new house, a city, or a village, entering them, the consecration of a deity, buying and selling, sacrifice (*yajña*), study, fire-offerings (*homa*), propitiatory rites (*śāntika*), nourishing rites (*pauṣṭika*), and matters concerning wealth, grain, tanks, and so forth. The qualities of one born in this asterism are: handsome, fond of sexual pleasure, capable, skillful, wealthy in grain, fond of various clothes, afflicted with eye disease, somewhat destitute, suffering from chronic catarrh (*pīnasa*), having small feet, hands, shoulders, and forehead, an enemy to his maternal uncle, and a maximum lifespan of eighty-eight years. Other details of this kind should be sought in this treatise. 1.
297. Now, regarding the lunar mansion Mṛgaśīrṣa: his form is white in color; he is the Moon, two-armed, holding a boon-granting gesture and a staff.
Mounted upon a chariot drawn by ten horses, he rejoiced at the rising of the Mṛgaśīrṣa constellation.
White in color; Soma is the presiding deity. — (In the Nakṣatracūḍāmaṇi:

It is the means for auspicious vows, fire-offerings, charity, penance, and sacrifice; as well as for the commencement of agriculture, entering into trade, travel, shaving, and union with beloved ones.

One should perform rites for peace (*śānti*), the royal consecration (*nṛpābhiṣeka*), religious observances (*niyama*), worship of the gods, fire, and ancestors, as well as auspicious rites for pacification and nourishment (*pauṣṭika*), when conjoined with a lunar mansion favorable to the Moon. [The asterism] Mṛgaśiras has three stars. Its synonyms are *ve*, *vo*, *kā*, *kī*. Its color is white. It consists of three stars. Its shape is that of the head of a deer (*mṛgaśīrṣa*). It is neuter. Its group is the gods (*devagaṇa*). Its face is turned sideways. Its source is the female serpent (*sarpiṇī-yoni*). Its presiding deity is Soma. Its caste is that of those who live by service (*upajīva-jāti*). It is bipedal. Its gaze is dull. It is gentle. Its stars are even. Its location is a city. Its element is the wind-mandala (*vāyu-maṇḍala*). Its tree is the Khadira. Its bird is the cock. Its vowel is the syllable *ṛ*. Its caste is the lifeless (*nirjīva-jāti*). A person born under this asterism is a man-deer (*puruṣa-mṛga*). After fourteen *ghaṭikās*, there are four "poisonous" (*viṣa*) *nāḍīs*. Eating the meat of a deer brings good fortune on journeys to the east or north. In case of fever, there is danger to life, or death within a month. For its pacification, the procedure for the worship of the deity Soma is as follows: [one should offer] white cloth, white sandalwood, *kuṇḍa* flowers, *guggulu* incense, and an offering of *paramānna* (milk-rice). Having worshipped with the sixteen services (*ṣoḍaśopacāra*) using the mantra "vavo nava," one should offer oblations (*homa*) one hundred and eight times with clarified butter mixed with milk while reciting the *Gāyatrī* mantra. One should present an offering (*bali*) of milk-rice along with perfumes and garlands. Within a month, one becomes happy. Under this asterism, a woman experiencing her first menses will have a son. Under this asterism, the following auspicious rites are recommended: *puṃsavana*, *jātakarma*, naming ceremony (*nāmakaraṇa*), the first feeding (*annaprāśana*), tonsure (*caula*), initiation (*upanayana*), learning the alphabet, study of the Vedas and Shastras, the return home (*samāvartana*), oil massage, wearing new ornaments and clothes, entering a new house or village, agriculture, sowing seeds, and medical treatment. The qualities of one born under this asterism are: energetic by nature, fearful of sin, devoted to mother and father, independent, long-lived, endowed with modesty, broad-chested, pleasant-faced, gentle in speech, intelligent, somewhat harsh, large-armed, focused, and devoted to righteousness. His maximum lifespan is eighty-four years. Such details should be sought in this treatise. 1. *Śāntisnānanṛpābhiṣekaniyamāndevāgnipitrarcanaṃ kuryācchāṃtikapauṣṭikādi śubhadaṃ caṃdrarkṣabhe saṃyute ||* 1 || 2. *śiromṛgaśirāstrīṇi | ve vo kā kī mṛgaśirāḥ | śvetavarṇam | tritārā | mṛgaśīrṣākṛtiḥ || napuṃsakam | devagaṇaḥ | tiryaṅmukham | sarpiṇīyoniḥ | somodevatā | upajīvajātiḥ | dvipāt | maṃdalocanam | mṛduḥ | samatārā | sthānaṃpuram | vāyumaṃḍalam | khādiravṛkṣaḥ | kukkuṭapakṣī | ṛkārākṣarassvaraḥ | nirjīvajātiḥ || asminnakṣatre puruṣamṛgojātaḥ || caturdaśaghaṭikābhyaḥ paraṃ viṣanāḍyaścatasraḥ || mṛgamāṃsabhakṣaṇaṃkṛtvāpūrvottaraprayāṇe śubham | jvareprāṇabhayam | athavāmāsamariṣṭam ||* 3. *tacchāṃtyaisomadevatāpūjāvidhānam | śvetavastram | śvetacaṃdanam | kuṃdapuṣpam | gugguladhūpaḥ | paramānnanaivedyam | vavonava itimaṃtreṇaṣoḍaśopacāraissaṃpūjyakṣīramiśraghṛtenagāyatryā aṣṭottaraśataṃjuhuyāt | gaṃdhamālyaiḥ kṣīrodanaṃbaliṃharet | māsātsukhī bhavati ||* 4. *asminnakṣatre prathamarajasvalāputravatī bhavati ||* 5. *asminnakṣatrepuṃsavanajātakarmanāmakaraṇānnaprāśanacaulopanayanākṣaragrahaṇavedaśāstrābhyāsasamāvartanatailābhyaṃganavābharaṇāṃbaradhāraṇavāstūpakramagrāmapuragṛhādipraveśakṛṣibījāvāpanabhaiṣajya prabhṛtiśubhakāryāṇipraśastāni ||* 6. *asminnakṣatrejātaguṇāḥ - utsāhaśīlaḥ | pāpabhīruḥ | mātāpitṛbhaktaḥ | svataṃtraḥ | cirāyuḥ | vinayasapannaḥ | pīnavakṣāḥ | sumukhaḥ | mṛduvacanaḥ | medhāvī | adhikanaiṣṭhuryavān | vipulabhujaḥ | ekagrāhī | dharmarataḥ | caturaśītivarṣāṇiparamāyurityādikamasmingraṃthe draṣṭavyam ||* 1 ||
298. Now, regarding the lunar mansion Ārdrā: Rudra is white, mounted upon a bull, adorned with white garlands, and four-armed.
May she who holds a trident, a sword, and the gestures of fearlessness and boon-granting be pleased. || 1 ||
White in color; Rudra is the presiding deity. — (In the Nakṣatracūḍāmaṇi:

It brings about the destruction of enemies, burning with the fire of the god of death, the crushing of the foremost among the wicked, the seizing of weapons and missiles, as well as theft, illicit travel, and the interception of messengers.

One should perform the rites for the command of the hosts of Rākṣasas, Bhūtas, Piśācas, Yakṣas, and Kinnaras, as well as exorcism (uccāṭana) and whatever other fierce rituals involving offerings have been taught, using either a fierce or a moist frog. || 1 ||

Ārdrā consists of one star. Its sound is *kū-ghaṃ-ṅaccha*. It is red in color. It has one star. It is feminine. Its group is that of humans. Its womb is the bitch. It is quadrupedal. It is fierce. Its face is turned upward. Its eye is in the middle. Its caste is Kṣatriya. Its place is empty. Its mandala is that of Varuṇa. Its deity is Rudra. Its tree is the red Khadira. Its bird is the Krauñca. Its vowel is the letter *e*. Beyond twenty-one *ghaṭikās*, there are four poisonous *nāḍīs*; travel during these should be avoided. Alternatively, after fourteen *ghaṭikās*, drinking the blood of a deer while traveling toward the east or north is auspicious. In cases of fever, there is danger to life, or else death within a month. The procedure for its pacification is the worship of Rudra. One should offer white cloth, white sandalwood paste, *dhuttūra* flowers, *bilva* leaves, and incense of *mahiṣākṣī-guggulu* or *agaru*. The food offering (*naivedya*) consists of various kinds of cooked rice. One should worship with the sixteen services (*ṣoḍaśopacāra*) using the mantra "Namaḥ te rudra" or "Namaḥ śambhave," and then perform one hundred and eight oblations of sesame seeds with the Gāyatrī mantra. One should present offerings of perfumes, garlands, and milk-rice (*kṣīrodana*). A white cow should be gifted. Within a month, one becomes well. Under this asterism, a woman experiencing her first menstruation becomes sorrowful. Under this asterism, cruel activities are recommended: the use of weapons, missiles, and fire; learning letters; practicing with weapons; going on thievery; the expulsion of spirits (*uccāṭana*); the employment of mantras and yantras; the consecration of Śaiva deities; possession by spirits; and the performance of ancestral rites (*śrāddha*). The qualities of one born under this asterism are: devoted to good conduct, skilled in buying and selling, brave, quarrelsome, injurious, ungrateful, having few enemies, and possessing a stable lifespan. His maximum lifespan is eighty-seven years. All such details are to be found in this entire treatise. 1.
Now, regarding the Punarvasu constellation:
Aditi is yellow in color and holds a *sruk* and *sruva* ladle, an axle, and a water-pot (*kamaṇḍalu*).
May she who bears an auspicious mark and is named after the Punarvasu constellation grant prosperity.
Yellow in color; Aditi is the deity. — (In the Nakṣatracūḍāmaṇi). —

The parting of the hair (*sīmantonnayana*), the rite for a male child (*puṃsavana*), rites for prosperity (*pauṣṭika*), the tonsure (*caula*), the investiture of the sacred thread (*mauñjī*), the vows regarding the Vedas (*vedavrata*), and various types of study are highly recommended.

Furthermore, one should certainly perform the preparation of swings (*āndolikā*) and other such items, as well as excellent vehicles, weapons, beds, and ornaments during the asterism of Aditi (Puṣya). || 1 ||

**Punarvasu:** Five stars; *ke*, *ko*, *hā*, *hi*, *punarvasū*; black in color; five stars; shaped like a house-pole (*gṛhadaṇḍa*); masculine; belonging to the group of gods; origin from the Mārjālīya fire-altar; Aditi is the presiding deity; Vaiśya caste; three feet; face turned sideways; beautiful eyes; movable station; a city; wind element (*vāyumaṇḍala*); bamboo tree; the swan as its bird; the letter *ṅa* is its vowel-sound. In this asterism, the Surabhi plant was born. Beyond twenty *ghaṭikās*, there are four poisonous *nāḍīs*. Drinking milk during travel toward the east or north brings auspiciousness. In cases of fever, there is danger for seven days. For its pacification, the ritual for the worship of Aditi is as follows: yellow cloth; saffron scent; white water-lily (*kumuda*) or jasmine (*mallikā*) flowers; sandalwood incense; an offering (*naivedya*) of rice cooked with molasses. Having worshipped her with the sixteen services using the mantra "Aditirdyauḥ," one should offer oblations (*homa*) one hundred and eight times with clarified butter, sesame, and rice while reciting the Gāyatrī. One should present an offering of rice with molasses along with perfumes and garlands. Within seven days, one becomes well. In this asterism, a woman experiences her first menstruation and gains the affection of many people. In this asterism, the following auspicious rites are recommended: conception ceremonies (*ṛtu*), male-impregnation rites (*puṃsavana*), the parting of the hair (*sīmantonnayana*), naming (*nāmakaraṇa*), the first feeding (*annaprāśana*), ear-piercing (*karṇavedha*), tonsure (*caula*), initiation (*upanayana*), learning the alphabet, study of the Vedas and Shastras, wearing fine clothes and ornaments, royal consecration, ascending the throne or a palanquin, decorating the bed, commencing a new residence, entering a city, village, or cave, journeys, and medical treatments. The qualities of one born in this asterism are: long-lived; beloved by women; handsome; desirous of wealth; of dull intellect; prominent; weak-voiced; fond of meat; intelligent; marked with a fish on the abdomen; a maximum lifespan of ninety-six years, and so forth—this should be seen in detail in this work. (1)
300. Now, regarding the Puṣya asterism:
one should worship Bṛhaspati, the deity of Puṣya, in human form.
With devotion, [he saw] the minister of the god, endowed with all ornaments. || 1 ||
Yellow in color; Jupiter is the presiding deity. (In the *Nakṣatracūḍāmaṇi*):

Under the Puṣya asterism, one should perform the study of the Vedas, the method of collecting excellent treatises, the practice of weapons and missiles, the recitation of mantras, the worship of deities, medical treatments, and audiences with kings. Likewise, one should perform rites for peace and prosperity, the royal procession, and the consecration of a king, as well as the wearing of fine, variegated garments and ornaments. (1)
Puṣya, sarala, and trīṇi—these three.

HŪ HE HO ḌĀ PUṢYA. White in color. Three stars. Arrow-shaped. Male. Belonging to the class of gods (Devagaṇa). Unborn source (Ajāyoni). Bṛhaspati is the presiding deity. Kṣatriya caste. Four-footed. Facing upward. Blind in one eye. Swift. External. Equal in number of stars. Location: a village. Fire-mandala. Aśvattha tree. Bird: water-crow. Vowel: the letter 'A'. In this asterism, those born are like lotuses and possess the luster of Venus. Beyond twenty ghaṭikās, there are four poisonous nāḍīs. After consuming excellent food, traveling in any direction is auspicious. For one afflicted by fever, there is danger for seven days. To pacify this, the procedure for the worship of Bṛhaspati is as follows: yellow cloth, saffron-scented paste, lotus flowers, agaru incense, and an offering of sugar, circular cakes, and boiled rice. Having worshipped with the sixteen services using the mantra "Bṛhaspate atiyadaryo arhāḥ," one should offer oblations one hundred and eight times with the Gāyatrī mantra using excellent food. One should present an offering of milk-rice along with perfumes and garlands. Within seven days, one becomes well. Under this asterism, a woman experiencing her first menses becomes devoted to her husband and blessed with sons. Under this asterism, the following are recommended: conception rites (Ṛtu), the Pumsavana rite, the Sīmantonnayana, naming ceremonies, the first feeding of solid food (Annaprāśana), ear-piercing, tonsure, the initiation ceremony (Caula/Upanayana), study of the Vedas and Shastras, instruction in mantras and yantras, oil massage, wearing new clothes and ornaments, the coronation of kings, the throne, the fourfold army, riding in palanquins, training and mounting elephants and horses, the commencement of building sites, entering cities, houses, and villages, sacrificial grounds, the instructions of gurus, great festivals, practice of instrumental music and dance, propitiatory (Śāntika) and nourishing (Pauṣṭika) rites, taking servants, buying and selling cattle, agricultural activities, sowing seeds, rituals, and the administration of medicine. The qualities of one born under this asterism are: omniscient, intelligent, quick to anger, possessing knowledge and inclination toward astrology, preeminent, courageous, helpful to kinsmen, sweet-spoken, a knower of mantras, proud, long-lived, subtle in speech, fond of solitude, marked with fish on the hands and feet, and having a maximum lifespan of ninety years. All such details are to be found in this treatise. 1.
301. Now, regarding the asterism Āśleṣā:
[the deity is] a serpent, red in color, with three eyes, and holding a shield and a sword in his two hands.
May the hand of the Bestower of Boons, which wears yellow garments and has Āśleṣā as its presiding deity, protect me. || 1 ||
[The deity] is red in color; the serpent is the presiding deity. (In the *Nakṣatracūḍāmaṇi*):

One should perform the application of mantras, malevolent rites (*abhicāra*), arson, physical exertion, verbal disputes, the ripening of the fruits of karma, the grasping of spears, swords, javelins, arrows, and bows, as well as the employment of poisons, indeed during the asterism of the Serpent (*Sārpa*).

Āśleṣā is shaped like a serpent. Its seed-syllables are *ḍī*, *ḍū*, *ḍe*, *ḍo*. It is Āśleṣā. Its color is red. It consists of six stars. Its form is that of a serpent. Its gender is feminine. Its group is the Rākṣasas. Its source is the womb of a cat. Its presiding deity is the Serpent. Its caste is Caṇḍāla. It has four feet. It faces downward. Its eyes are dull. It is fierce. It is external. It has half a star. Its place is empty. Its mandala is that of Varuṇa. Its tree is the Punnāga. Its bird is the Ṭiṭṭibha. In this asterism, Dharmarāja (Yama) was born. Beyond thirty-two *ghaṭikās*, there are four poisonous *nāḍīs*; travel during these is forbidden. Alternatively, after fourteen *ghaṭikās*, if one eats excellent food and sets out toward the east or north, it is auspicious. In case of fever, there is danger to life, or death within a month. For its pacification, the procedure for worshiping the deity Serpent is as follows: [Offer] honey-colored cloth; saffron and agallochum (*agaru*) as fragrance; Agasti flowers; ghee and *guggulu* as incense; milk-rice (*pāyasa*) as the food offering. Having performed the sixteen-fold worship with the mantra "Obeisance to the Serpents" (*namostu sarpebhyaḥ*), one should offer oblations one hundred and eight times with clarified butter mixed with excellent food while reciting the Gāyatrī mantra. One should present an offering of milk-rice along with perfumes and garlands. A red cow should be gifted. After a month, one becomes well. In this asterism, a woman who experiences her first menstruation becomes ill-behaved. In this asterism, the practice of striking, the application of poisons or fire, the use of spells, speech-weapons, bows and other weapons, the employment of mantras, illicit intercourse with another's wife, and the construction of wells, small tanks, large tanks, bells, iron bars, and so forth, are all commended. The qualities of one born in this asterism: honored by kings; fierce; lustful; a wanderer; marked on the body with sesame seeds and fish; having extensive sexual pleasure; slow-moving; a serpent-like person. His maximum lifespan is eighty-six years. All such details are to be found in this entire treatise. 1.
302. Now, regarding the Maghā constellation:
the ancestors have sacrificial cakes (*piṇḍa*) in their hands; they are emaciated, smoke-colored, and pure.
May the deities of the Maghā constellation grant us what is auspicious.
Smoke-colored; the ancestors are the deities. — (In the *Nakṣatracūḍāmaṇi*):
One should perform the establishment of the sacred fire (*agnyādhāna*), the application of all mantras, the ancestral offering (*śrāddha*), and the libation (*tarpaṇa*) for the ancestors.
The commencement of gambling, the doctrine of karma, a hole, ancestral rites, liquor, battle, and the discharge of weapons. || 1 ||

Maghā consists of five stars: mā, mī, mū, me, and maghā. Its color is black. It has five stars. Its shape is like the pole of a swing (āṃdolikā). It faces downward. It is masculine and feminine. Its attendant host is the Rākṣasas. Its source of birth is the mouse. Its presiding deities are the Pitṛs. Its social class is Śūdra. It has four feet. Its eye is in the middle. It is fierce. Its position is internal. Its stars are equal in size. Its location is a city. Its element is the fire-maṇḍala. Its tree is the banyan (vaṭa). Its bird is the cock. Its syllable is *ghasa*. Yama was born under this asterism. (p. 192)

Beyond thirty *ghaṭikās*, there are four *nāḍīs* of poison (*viṣanāḍī*); travel during these should be avoided. Alternatively, after eleven *ghaṭikās* and up until the twenty-second *ghaṭikā*, if one eats sesame seeds and then sets out on a journey toward the south or west, it is auspicious. If a fever occurs on a Sunday, there is danger to life; otherwise, for twenty days, there are portents of misfortune (*ariṣṭa*). To pacify this, the ritual for worshipping the ancestral deities (*pitṛdevatā*) is prescribed: black cloth, black agallochum (*kṛṣṇāgaru*) incense, *caṃpaka* flowers, incense of ghee, agallochum, and *guggulu*, and an offering (*naivedya*) of rice cooked in ghee and cakes. Having worshipped with the sixteen services (*ṣoḍaśopacāra*) using the mantra "udīratām avaraḥ," one should offer oblations (*homa*) one hundred and eight times with *gāyatrī* using rice mixed with sesame and clarified butter. One should present an offering of sesame-rice along with perfumes and garlands. A black cow should be given as a gift. After twenty days, one becomes well. Under this asterism (*nakṣatra*), a woman experiencing her first menses becomes sorrowful. Under this asterism, the following are recommended: the return ceremony (*samāvartana*), marriage, the application of all mantras and tantras, becoming a king, the acquisition or purchase of female slaves, buying and selling, plowing, sowing seeds, gambling, deposits, collyrium, giving away a daughter in marriage, the employment of mechanical devices, the construction of wells, tanks, and ponds, *śrāddha* rites, and the libations (*tarpaṇa*) to the ancestors. The qualities of one born under this asterism are: learned, devoted to discipline, devoted to father and mother, possessing many virtues, long-lived, wealthy, skilled in affairs, a benefactor to kinsmen, clear-spoken, a subduer of enemy hosts, of limited intellect, prone to quick illness, fond of his own wife, red-eyed, marked by a fish on the abdomen, and having a maximum lifespan of ninety-seven years. All such details should be sought in this entire treatise. 1.
303. Now, regarding the Pūrvaphālgunī constellation: I worship Aryaman, the deity of the Phalgunī stars—smoke-colored, mounted upon a chariot, and joined with a hand holding a fine spear. (1)
The deity is Aryaman. His color is smoky-grey. — (In the Nakṣatracūḍāmaṇi)

One should perform that which is ordained for entering a city, attacking a fortress, administering poison, [dealing with] fear, disease, and suffering, as well as mantras, medicines, the science of Garuḍa, mining, and matters concerning fortune. Regarding Pūrvaphalgunī and Uttaraphalgunī: both have two stars each; they are called Khaṭvācoka. For Pūrvaphalgunī: the syllables are *mo ṭā ṭī ṭū*; its color is white; it has two stars; its shape is like a staff (*daṇḍa*); its gender is feminine; its group is human; its source is the mouse; its presiding deity is Bhaga; its caste is Brahmin; it is four-footed; it faces downward; it has beautiful eyes; it is fierce; its position is internal; its star-measure is equal; its place is a village; its element is fire; its bird is the vulture; its tree is the *pālāśa*; its sound is a vowel.

Beyond twenty *ghaṭikās*, there are four *nāḍīs* (periods) of poison; these must be avoided for a journey. Alternatively, after eighteen *ghaṭikās*, it is auspicious for departure. However, in the case of fever, there is danger to life. Or else, the *ariṣṭa* (fatal sign) lasts for one month, nine days, or two months. For its pacification, there is a procedure for the worship of the deity Aryaman: a red cloth, red sandalwood paste, and worship with sixteen services (*ṣoḍaśopacāra*) using the mantra "Aryamaṇam" with red *karavīra* flowers, *bilva* incense, and an offering of *kṛsarā* rice. One should then perform a hundred and eight oblations of black gram porridge mixed with clarified butter while reciting the *Gāyatrī*. One should present an offering (*bali*) of fragrant garlands and *priyaṅgu* rice. After a month, one becomes well. Under this asterism (*nakṣatra*), a woman experiencing her first menstruation becomes bereft of husband and sons. In this asterism, activities such as the practice of letters, the study of scriptures, and the application of poisons or fire are recommended. The qualities of one born under this asterism are: handsome, self-controlled, beloved by the world and the people, fond of song and instrumental music, adorned with ornaments, fond of study, fickle, and motherless. His maximum lifespan is ninety years. All such details are to be found in this entire work. 1.
304. Now, regarding the constellation Uttarāphalgunī:
[the deity] Bhaga is mounted upon an excellent chariot, has two arms, and holds a conch and a discus.
I meditate upon the deity Phalgunī, who bestows the desired boons upon her devotees. || 1 ||
Red in color; the deity is Bhaga. (From the *Nakṣatracūḍāmaṇi*):

Wells, step-wells, ponds, large lakes, cities, palaces, temples, beds, jewels, ornaments, bodily decoration, the use of a throne, bathing, anointing, auspicious rites, marriage, the consecration of a king, as well as the commencement of agriculture and the entry into a city—all these activities should be performed under the asterism Ārdrā.

Pūrvaphalgunī and Uttaraphalgunī consist of two stars each, forming a couch (*khaṭvā*). Their seed-syllables are *ṭe* and *ṭo*, and their presiding deity is Pāpī. Their color is red; they consist of two stars and are shaped like a staff. They are female, belong to the human class, have cattle as their source, and Bhaga is their presiding deity. They are of the Kṣatriya caste, possess three feet, face upward, and have blind eyes. They are fixed, located at the end, and contain slightly more than half a star. Their place is empty, their tree is the *badarī*, their bird is the heron (*kaṅka*), and their syllable is *jarā*. Jupiter was born under this asterism. Beyond eighteen *ghaṭikās*, there are four poisonous *nāḍīs*. It is auspicious to travel toward the southwest after eating vegetables and meat. In cases of fever, seven days are unfavorable. To pacify these, one should perform the ritual worship of the deity Bhaga.

Saffron fragrance; blue lotus flower; *bilva* incense; an offering (*naivedya*) of red *śāli* rice; having worshipped with the sixteen services (*ṣoḍaśopacāra*) using the mantra "Bhagapraṇeta," one should offer oblations of food mixed with ghee while reciting the *Gāyatrī* mantra one hundred and eight times, and then present an offering (*bali*) of fragrant garlands and rice cooked in ghee. Within a month, one becomes happy. Under this asterism, a woman experiencing her first menstrual period becomes the mother of a son. Under this asterism, the following auspicious and stable rites are recommended: the *Kratu*, *Puṃsavana*, *Sīmantonnayana*, naming ceremony (*nāmakaraṇa*), first feeding (*annaprāśana*), ear-piercing (*karṇavedha*), tonsure (*caula*), initiation (*upanayana*), marriage (*vivāha*), graduation (*samāvartana*), the binding of garments, ornaments, and turbans, the mounting of thrones and swings, the entry into cities, villages, houses, and so forth, Vedic study, sacrifices, sowing seeds, and the decoration of archways (*toraṇa*). The qualities of one born under this asterism are: a poetic disposition, prideful, knower of dharma, fortunate, skillful, excellent, lustful toward women, prone to illness, dark-complexioned, fond of discipline, possessing little happiness, learned, marked with a fish on the body, and having a maximum lifespan of eighty-four years—all such details should be sought in this entire treatise. 1.
305 Now, regarding the lunar mansion Hastā:
I pay homage to Savitṛ, whose vehicle is a chariot drawn by seven horses.
[One should worship] the Lord of the Shadow (Chāyeśa), the deity of the Hasta constellation, seated in the lotus posture (padmāsana). || 1 ||
Red in color; the deity is Savitṛ. — [In the *Nakṣatracūḍāmaṇi*:
Taking of the hand in marriage and other rites, offerings, auspicious ceremonies, journeys, royal consecration, and the consecration of houses, palaces, and deities.
Let the learned man perform all activities, such as agriculture and exertion, [providing] garments like variegated cloth, excellent vehicles, and ornaments. || 1 ||

The Hasta nakṣatra has the form of a hand; its arrows are the Pūṣaṇas. Its letter is *ḍha*; its color is black; it consists of five stars; its shape is that of a hand; it is masculine; its group is the Devas; its source is the buffalo; its presiding deity is Sūrya; its caste is Vaiśya; it has four feet; its face is turned sideways; it is light; its eyes are dull; it is swift; its position is internal; its place is a city; its element is the wind-maṇḍala; its tree is the Ambaṣṭha; its bird is the parrot; its syllable is *lā*; its deity is Sūrya. In this nakṣatra, the Nakula and Sahadeva snakes are born. Beyond twenty-one ghaṭikās, there are four poisonous nāḍīs. It is auspicious for traveling in all directions after consuming rice. In the case of fever, there is danger to life, or else misfortune (*ariṣṭa*) lasts for fifteen days. For its pacification, there is the ritual for the worship of the deity Savitṛ: red cloth, red sandalwood paste, red karavīra flowers, ten-ingredient incense (*daśāṅga-dhūpa*), and offerings of cakes (*apūpa*).

(p. 195) The Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara, while practicing the profound *prajñāpāramitā*, perceives that the five aggregates are all empty and thereby delivers all suffering beings. Śāriputra, form is emptiness; emptiness itself is form. Form is not different from emptiness; emptiness is not different from form. What is form is emptiness; what is emptiness is form. The same applies to feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness. Śāriputra, all phenomena are marked by emptiness. They have no characteristics, no birth, no cessation, no defilement, no purity, no decrease, and no increase. Śāriputra, because form is empty, there is no form; because feeling is empty, there is no feeling; because perception is empty, there is no perception; because mental formations are empty, there are no mental formations; and because consciousness is empty, there is no consciousness. Śāriputra, because all phenomena are empty, they are devoid of characteristics: they are without birth, without cessation, without defilement, without purity, without decrease, and without increase. Therefore, Śāriputra, in emptiness there is no form, no feeling, no perception, no mental formations, and no consciousness; no eye, no ear, no nose, no tongue, no body, and no mind; no form, no sound, no smell, no taste, no touchable object, and no phenomenon; no realm of sight up to and including no realm of mind-consciousness; no ignorance and no extinction of ignorance, up to and including no old age and death and no extinction of old age and death; no suffering, no origin, no cessation, and no path; no wisdom and no attainment. Because there is nothing to attain, a Bodhisattva relies on the *prajñāpāramitā* and dwells with a mind free from obstacles. Because there are no obstacles, he has no fear. Having transcended all inverted dreams, he attains ultimate *nirvāṇa*. All Buddhas of the three times, relying on the *prajñāpāramitā*, fully awaken to unsurpassed, complete, and perfect enlightenment. Therefore, know that the *prajñāpāramitā* is a great spiritual mantra, a great bright mantra, a supreme mantra, and an unequaled mantra. It relieves all suffering and is true, not false. Thus, the mantra of *prajñāpāramitā* should be proclaimed: Gate gate pāragate pārasaṃgate bodhi svāhā. (p. 196) At that time, the Buddha spoke these verses: Form is not different from emptiness; emptiness is not different from form. Form is precisely emptiness; emptiness is precisely form. The same applies to feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness. All phenomena are empty in nature; they are neither born nor extinguished, neither defiled nor pure, neither increasing nor decreasing. Therefore, in emptiness there is no form, no feeling, no perception, no mental formations, and no consciousness. No eye, ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind; no form, sound, smell, taste, touch, or phenomenon. No realm of sight up to and including no realm of mind-consciousness. No ignorance and no extinction of ignorance, up to and including no old age and death and no extinction of old age and death. No suffering, no origin, no cessation, and no path. No wisdom and no attainment. Because there is nothing to attain, a Bodhisattva relies on the *prajñāpāramitā* and dwells with a mind free from obstacles. Because there are no obstacles, he has no fear. Having transcended all inverted dreams, he attains ultimate *nirvāṇa*. All Buddhas of the three times, relying on the *prajñāpāramitā*, fully awaken to unsurpassed, complete, and perfect enlightenment. Therefore, know that the *prajñāpāramitā* is a great spiritual mantra, a great bright mantra, a supreme mantra, and an unequaled mantra. It relieves all suffering and is true, not false. Thus, the mantra of *prajñāpāramitā* should be proclaimed: Gate gate pāragate pārasaṃgate bodhi svāhā. // Chapter on the Heart of *Prajñāpāramitā*, the Twenty-Fifth. // (p. 197) // Chapter on the Practice of the Path, the Twenty-Sixth. // At that time, the Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha: “World-Honored One, how should a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva practice the *prajñāpāramitā*? The Buddha told Subhūti: “A Bodhisattva Mahāsattva should thus practice the *prajñāpāramitā*: he should contemplate all phenomena as empty and signless. He should not dwell on the notion of form, nor dwell on the notions of feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness. He should not dwell on the notion of the eye, nor dwell on the notions of the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind. He should not dwell on the notion of form, nor dwell on the notions of sound, smell, taste, touchable objects, or phenomena. He should not dwell on the notion of the realm of sight, nor dwell on the notions of the realms of hearing, smelling, tasting, touching, or mind-consciousness. He should not dwell on the notion of ignorance, nor dwell on the notions of the extinction of ignorance, up to and including the notion of old age and death and the extinction of old age and death. He should not dwell on the notion of suffering, nor dwell on the notions of the origin, cessation, or path. He should not dwell on the notion of wisdom, nor dwell on the notion of attainment. Why is this? Subhūti, if a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva dwells on the notion of form, he does not practice the *prajñāpāramitā*. If he dwells on the notions of feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness, he does not practice the *prajñāpāramitā*. If he dwells on the notion of the eye, he does not practice the *prajñāpāramitā*. If he dwells on the notions of the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind, he does not practice the *prajñāpāramitā*. If he dwells on the notion of form, he does not practice the *prajñāpāramitā*. If he dwells on the notions of sound, smell, taste, touchable objects, or phenomena, he does not practice the *prajñāpāramitā*. If he dwells on the notion of the realm of sight, he does not practice the *prajñāpāramitā*. If he dwells on the notions of the realms of hearing, smelling, tasting, touching, or mind-consciousness, he does not practice the *prajñāpāramitā*. If he dwells on the notion of ignorance, he does not practice the *prajñāpāramitā*. If he dwells on the notions of the extinction of ignorance, up to and including the notion of old age and death and the extinction of old age and death, he does not practice the *prajñāpāramitā*. If he dwells on the notion of suffering, he does not practice the *prajñāpāramitā*. If he dwells on the notions of the origin, cessation, or path, he does not practice the *prajñāpāramitā*. If he dwells on the notion of wisdom, he does not practice the *prajñāpāramitā*. If he dwells on the notion of attainment, he does not practice the *prajñāpāramitā*. Why is this? Subhūti, if a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva does not dwell on the notion of form, he practices the *prajñāpāramitā*. If he does not dwell on the notions of feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness, he practices the *prajñāpāramitā*. If he does not dwell on the notion of the eye, he practices the *prajñāpāramitā*. If he does not dwell on the notions of the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind, he practices the *prajñāpāramitā*. If he does not dwell on the notion of form, he practices the *prajñāpāramitā*. If he does not dwell on the notions of sound, smell, taste, touchable objects, or phenomena, he practices the *prajñāpāramitā*. If he does not dwell on the notion of the realm of sight, he practices the *prajñāpāramitā*. If he does not dwell on the notions of the realms of hearing, smelling, tasting, touching, or mind-consciousness, he practices the *prajñāpāramit

Having worshipped with the *ud ityam iti* mantra using the sixteen types of offerings (*ṣoḍaśopacāra*), one should offer oblations of *arka* wood and clarified butter one hundred and eight times while reciting the *Gāyatrī*. Then, one should present an offering (*bali*) of black gram (*māṣa*) cooked rice along with perfumes and garlands. Within fifteen days, one becomes happy. Under this asterism (*nakṣatra*), a woman experiencing her first menses will have a son. Under this asterism, the following are recommended: the *puṃsavana* rite, the first feeding (*annaprāśana*), ear-piercing, tonsure (*caula*), initiation (*upanayana*), study of the Vedas and Shastras, the return home (*samāvartana*), marriage, oil massage, wearing new clothes and ornaments, rites for peace (*śāntika*) and prosperity (*pauṣṭika*), great festivals, riding in a palanquin, chariot, or horse, the buying and selling of livestock, the commencement of agriculture, sowing seeds, the collection of grain, wearing new garments, the acquisition of excellent gems, and journeys for the purpose of mantras, scriptures, or medicine. The qualities of one born under this asterism are as follows: he is famous, eloquent, possessed of the wealth of many scriptures, skillful, wealthy, fond of women, devoted to his own wife, intent on the welfare of others' affairs, a worshiper of Brahmins and gurus, renowned, a destroyer of enemies, yet a stealer of his wife's property; his body is marked with the sign of a fish; his maximum lifespan is eighty-eight years. Such details are to be found in this work. 1.
306. Now, regarding the Citrā constellation:
[one should meditate on] Tvaṣṭṛ, the deity of the Citrā constellation, mounted upon a chariot.
I worship Him who wears a crown and whose hands are adorned with the conch and the discus.
Red in color; Tvaṣṭṛ is the presiding deity. — (In the *Nakṣatracūḍāmaṇi*):
Variegated garments, ornaments, and decorations; variegated craftsmanship; pearls and gems for the ears; and coral.
The duties of Tvaṣṭṛ include the initiatory rites (*upanayana*), the practice of shaving (*kṣurakarma*), and the arts of singing, dancing, various crafts, and instrumental music. || 1 ||

Citrā: one *mauktika* (pearl). *Pe*, *po*, *rā*, *rī*—Citrā. White color. One star (*tārā*). Pearl-shaped. Male gender. Associated with the *rākṣasa* class. Tiger as its source (*yoni*). Tvaṣṭṛ as its presiding deity (*devatā*). Artisan class (*upajīvijāti*). Two-legged. Facing obliquely. Eyes in the middle. Soft. External. Equal star. Location is a city (*pattana*). Air element (*vāyumaṇḍala*). Bilva tree. Bird is the crow. The syllable is *ṭa*. Poisonous hours (*viṣanāḍī*) are four after twenty *ghaṭikās*; travel during these is to be avoided. Alternatively, it is auspicious for a journey toward the south or west after eating Citrā-rice at fourteen *ghaṭikās*. In cases of fever, there is danger for eleven days. For its pacification, the procedure for worship of the deity Tvaṣṭṛ is as follows: variegated cloth; saffron scent; variegated flowers; resin of *sarja* as incense; sweetmeats (*modaka*) as the food offering (*naivedya*). Having worshipped with the sixteen services (*ṣoḍaśopacāra*) using the mantra "Citraṃ devānām," one should offer one hundred and eight oblations of Citrā-rice mixed with clarified butter while reciting the Gāyatrī mantra. Then, one should present an offering (*bali*) of Citrā-rice along with perfumes and garlands.

After eleven days, she becomes comfortable. Under this asterism (*nakṣatra*), a woman who has reached her first menses becomes capable [of performing auspicious rites]. Under this asterism, for a woman, the following auspicious activities are recommended: the naming ceremony (*nāmakaraṇa*), the first feeding of solid food (*annaprāśana*), the piercing of the ears (*karṇavedha*), the tonsure (*caula*), the initiation (*upanayana*), the learning of letters, the study of the Vedas and Śāstras, the application of oil massages (*tailābhyaṅga*), the wearing of variegated garments and various ornaments, the protection and tethering of elephants and horses, training in chariots and other arts, dancing, the concealment of divine [images], the concealment of women, painting and various other crafts, the commencement of various branches of knowledge, the cultivation of various plants and medicinal herbs, and the administration of medicines. The qualities of one born under this asterism are: being fond of wealth, possessing enjoyments, being amorous, and having a maximum lifespan of eighty-four years; all such details are to be found in this treatise. (1)
307 Now, regarding the Svāti constellation: [one should worship] Vāyu, the deity of the Svāti constellation, who is mounted upon a deer.
I bow to him who has a smoky complexion and whose hands shine with a sword and shield. || 1 ||
Smoke-colored; Vāyu is the presiding deity. — (In the *Nakṣatracūḍāmaṇi*):
The establishment of crops, gardens, cities, celestial abodes, houses, and palaces; and mounting upon swaying swings, comfortable seats, camels, horses, and shoulders.

The wise declare that under the wind (Māruta) asterism, there is success in the commencement of learning, marriage, rites for prosperity, trade, agriculture, and other such undertakings, as well as in obtaining various garments, ornaments, and bodily adornments. || 1 ||

Svātī is a single ruby (*māṇikya*). Its seed-syllable is *rū*, *re*, or *ro*. Its color is red. It consists of a single star. It has the luster of coral. Its presiding group of deities is the *devagaṇa*. Its source is the buffalo (*mahiṣī*). Its presiding deity is Vāyu (the Wind). Its caste is Śūdra. It is four-footed. It moves last. Its face is turned sideways. It possesses beautiful eyes. Its location is empty. Its element is the wind-mandala (*vāyumaṇḍala*). Its tree is the Arjuna. Its bird is the hawk (*śyena*). Its syllable is the letter *va*. After fourteen *ghaṭikās*, there are four poisonous *nāḍīs* (hours); travel during these should be avoided. Alternatively, after fourteen *ghaṭikās*, if one eats ground *āmalaka* fruit before setting out toward the south or west, it is auspicious. In this asterism, Nṛsiṃha was born. During a fever, there is danger to life, or else death within a month. To pacify this, one should perform the ritual worship of the presiding deity Vāyu. The fragrance is black agallochum (*kṛṣṇāguru*). The flower is *mādhavī*. The incense is black agallochum. The food offering (*naivedya*) is curd-rice. Having worshipped with the sixteen services using the mantra "tadvāyavṛtaspate," one should offer oblations (*homa*) one hundred and eight times with parched grain and clarified butter while reciting the Gāyatrī mantra. One should present an offering of curd-rice along with perfumes and garlands. Within a month, one becomes happy. In this asterism, a woman experiencing her first menstrual period becomes virtuous, fortunate, and endowed with good fortune.

In this asterism, auspicious activities such as sexual union with a woman, naming ceremonies (*nāmakaraṇa*), the first feeding of solid food (*annaprāśana*), the tonsure ceremony (*caula*), the initiation into sacred study (*upanayana*), the acquisition of letters, the study of astrology and other sciences, the return home after studies (*samāvartana*), marriage, oil massages, wearing new garments, putting on pearl ornaments, the commencement of dancing, singing, and instrumental music, mounting elephants, horses, or swings, the construction of palaces and the like, the commencement of agriculture, and the sowing of seeds are all highly recommended. The qualities of one born in this asterism are: fortunate, self-controlled, generous, courageous, tall-limbed, handsome-bodied, large-eyed, possessing a heart of diverse character, famous, prone to anger, devoted to the worship of the twice-born, gurus, and deities, a spender of wealth, dear to kinsmen, poetic in nature, very clever, fond of laughter, independent, and having a maximum lifespan of ninety years. All such details are to be found in this entire treatise. (1)
308. Now, regarding the Viśākhā asterism: Indra and Agni are its presiding deities; if they are auspicious, Viśākhā will be auspicious.
I bow to the two who are mounted upon a single chariot, their lotus-like hands displaying the gestures of granting boons and fearlessness.

Agni is red in color; Indra is golden in color. The deities are Indra and Agni. — (In the *Nakṣatracūḍāmaṇi*): One should perform the wearing of jewels and gold ornaments, sacrifices, fire-offerings (*homa*), fasting, vows, fire-rituals, acts of affection, binding with cords, and so forth.

One should perform the worship of the world, the most excellent sages, the elements, the ritual actions, the two-fold destiny, the gods, the preceptor, and the ancestors during the asterisms presided over by Agni.

Viśākhā is the fifth lunar mansion (*nakṣatra*). Its symbol is the wheel of a potter. It consists of two stars; its color is red; it has five *tārās*; it is masculine; its presiding group (*gaṇa*) is the Rākṣasas; its face is downward; its eyes are blind; its source (*yoni*) is the tiger; it is common (*sādhāraṇa*); its syllable is *ga*; its tree is the *vikatavṛkṣa*; its bird is the *kāraṇḍava*; its deities are Indra and Agni; its caste is Kṣatriya; it has three feet; its stars are equal in number; its shape is that of an archway (*toraṇa*); its place is empty; its mandala is fire. Beyond fourteen *ghaṭikās*, there are four poisonous *nāḍīs*; travel during these should be avoided. In cases of fever, there is danger to life, or else misfortune (*ariṣṭa*) for fifteen days. For its pacification, the procedure for the worship of the deities Indra and Agni is as follows: [one should offer] a red garment, the eight fragrances (*aṣṭagaṃdha*), white flowers, incense of black agallochum (*kālāguru*), and an offering of cooked rice with red ginger. Having worshipped with the sixteen services (*ṣoḍaśopacāra*) using the *Tryambaka* mantra, one should perform a fire-oblation (*homa*) of food mixed with ghee one hundred and eight times while reciting the *Gāyatrī*. One should present an offering (*bali*) of red food together with wine. Thus, one becomes happy. A woman who first menstruates under this asterism becomes fortunate. [Text missing] The qualities of one born under this asterism: he is beloved by the learned, devoted to modesty, long-lived, wealthy, skillful in his undertakings, a benefactor to his circle of kinsmen, and endowed with many virtues.

He speaks clearly; he is a subduer of hosts of enemies; he possesses little intelligence; he is subject to quick diseases; he is captivating to the heart; he is fond of his own wife; his eyes are red; his abdomen is marked with fish; his maximum lifespan is ninety years—all such details as these are to be seen in this treatise. || 1 ||
309 Now, regarding the lunar mansion Anurādhā:
I worship Mitra, the Lord of Anurādhā, seated upon a lotus throne.
His pair of excellent arms hold a trident and a goad, and his complexion is the color of blood.
Red in color; Mitra is the presiding deity. (In the *Nakṣatracūḍāmaṇi*):
Painting, the examination of gold and jewels, and the breeding of horses, cattle, bulls, and elephants.

The application of powders, collyriums for the eyes, and medicinal treatments; journeys, marriages, and auspicious rites for prosperity—these are to be performed under the Maitra constellation. || 1 ||

Anurādhā consists of three stars: *nā*, *nī*, *nū*, *ne*. Its color is white. It has three stars. It is masculine. Its divine group is the Devas. Its shape is that of a flower. Its presiding deity is Mitra. Its social class is Śūdra. Its source is the deer (*hariṇī*). Its face is turned sideways. Its eyes are small. It is gentle. Its place is a city. Its mandala is that of Indra. Its tree is the Bakula. Its bird is the owl. Its syllable is *tha*. In this asterism, the Nandana grove was born. Beyond ten *ghaṭikās*, there are four poisonous *nāḍīs*. Eating horse-gram (*kulittha*) and setting out toward all directions brings auspiciousness. In case of fever, there is danger to life, or else death within a month. The procedure for the worship of the deity Mitra for its pacification is as follows: red cloth; saffron as perfume; fragrant flowers; bilva leaves; bilva incense; an offering of rice mixed with sesame (*kṛsarānna*); having worshipped with the sixteen services using the mantra "Devasya tvā," one should offer oblations one hundred and eight times with vegetables, roots, fruits, and clarified butter while reciting the Gāyatrī. One should present an offering of molasses-rice along with perfumes and garlands in the eastern direction. Within a month, one becomes happy. In this asterism, a woman experiencing her first menses will possess wealth and virtuous sons. In this asterism, the following rites are recommended: conception (*ṛtu*), the *puṃsavana* rite, the *sīmantonnayana*, naming, the first feeding of solid food (*annaprāśana*), ear-piercing, tonsure (*caula*), initiation (*upanayana*), study of the Vedas and Shastras, the return home (*samāvartana*), marriage, oil-massage, wearing new clothes, wearing new jewel ornaments, the coronation of a king, mounting a chariot or palanquin, the commencement of building a house, the installation of the ritual stake (*śaṅku*), entering a city or village, the beginning of dance, song, flute-playing, and instrumental music, the practice of arts and sciences, the collection of new jewels and animals, buying and selling, agricultural activities, sowing seeds, ancestral rites (*śrāddha*), and medical treatments. The qualities of one born in this asterism are: devoted to compassion, wise, and afflicted by hunger.

He is a bestower of auspiciousness; one who follows the true path; an enjoyer of pleasures; a granter of boons to kings and eminent persons; gracious; one who has few children; peaceful; a giver of food; renowned; honored by kings; under the influence of young women; residing in another land; and having a maximum lifespan of ninety years—all such details are to be found in this treatise.
Now, regarding the Jyeṣṭhā asterism:
One should visualize Indra in one's heart, mounted upon a white elephant, with his right hand holding a vajra and a goad, possessing a thousand eyes, and having a yellowish luster. (1)
Yellow in color; Indra is the deity. — ||
(In the *Nakṣatracūḍāmaṇi*):

The destruction of enemy cities, sowing dissension, acts of deception, the use of bows, swords, clubs, and other weapons, craftsmanship, and the performance of fire-offerings [are to be undertaken under these asterisms].
Deceit, crookedness, sorcery, punishment, malevolent magic, the seizing of wealth, and other matters proclaimed by Indra. || 1 ||

Jyeṣṭhā has three stars, shaped like an earring (*kuṇḍala*). Its presiding deity is Jyeṣṭhā; its color is white; it consists of three stars; its form is that of an earring; its gender is female; its attendant class is the *Rākṣasa* group; its source is the deer (*hariṇa*); its presiding deity is Indra; its livelihood is the artisan class (*upajīvijāti*); it is four-footed; its face is turned sideways; its eyes are in the middle; it is sharp; its position is empty; its mandala is that of Indra; its tree is the *śālmali*; its bird is the *cātaka*; its letters are *tha* and *kṣa*. Beyond fourteen *ghaṭikās*, there are four poisonous (*viṣa*) *nāḍīs*; travel during these should be avoided. Alternatively, after consuming curd, rice, and sesame, traveling toward the south or west is auspicious. In case of fever, there is danger to life, or else death within a month. For its pacification, the procedure for worshiping the deity Indra is as follows: yellow cloth, *śrīgandha* (sandalwood paste), *pāṭala* flowers, incense of camphor and *agaru*, and an offering of variegated rice (*citrānna*) as the food oblation. Having worshipped with the sixteen services using the mantra "indraṃ vo viśvatas pari," one should offer one hundred and eight oblations of variegated rice and clarified butter while reciting the *Gāyatrī*. Then, one should present a bali-offering of fragrant garlands and variegated rice. Within a month, one becomes well. A woman who first menstruates under this asterism will become poor, yet she shall have many sons. Under this asterism, acts of valor, the application of poison or fire, sorcery (*abhicāra*), the employment of yantras and mantras, battle, gambling, legal proceedings, theft, travel, liberation, paralyzing (*stambhana*), the study of scriptures, the exorcism of spirits and ghosts (*uccāṭana*), debates on knowledge, the seizing of women or others' property, and the buying and selling of livestock are all recommended. The qualities of one born under this asterism are: dark-complexioned, firm in grasping the hand (in marriage), devoted to learning, possessing many sons and friends, contented, truthful, lustful toward women, troubled, surrounded by a host of enemies, and quick to anger.

He will live a moderate life; he will be wealthy; he will be soft-spoken; he will be honored by kings; he will be a worshiper of the twice-born and his gurus; his body will be marked with sesame seeds and fish; he will be devoted to his own wife; and his maximum lifespan will be ninety-five years—all such details are to be found in this very treatise. || 1 ||
311. Now, regarding the Mūla constellation:
[one should visualize] a black Yātudhāna holding a sword and a shield, mounted upon a human being.
I worship the deity presiding over the root-mantra, who has upward-pointing hair and three uneven eyes. || 1 ||
Black in color; the Yātudhāna is its presiding deity.
(In the *Nakṣatracūḍāmaṇi*):
The planting of various shrubs, creepers, and trees, and the cultivation of mung beans, sugarcane, black gram, sesame, and mustard.

In the *Mūla* [chapter], there is the commencement of all sciences concerning mantras, medicinal herbs, weapons, scriptures, and tantras, as well as the selection of the bridegroom and the bride. || 1 ||

The *Mūlāṅkuśa* [constellation] consists of six stars. Its seed-syllables are *ye*, *yo*, *ba*, and *bī* (or *bhā*, *bhī*). It is black in color. It has six stars (*ṣaṭtārā*) and the shape of a goad (*aṅkuśākṛti*). Its presiding spirit is a lion (*siṃhātmavān*). It is neuter. It belongs to the class of *Rākṣasas*. Its source is the parrot (*śukayoni*). The deity is Nirṛti. Its nature is fierce (*dāruṇam*). It faces downward (*adhomukham*). It possesses beautiful eyes (*sulocanam*). It is at the end (*antaḥ*). It is even (*samam*). Its place is the city (*pattanam*). It is the Varuṇa-maṇḍala. Its tree is the Sarja (*sarjavṛkṣa*). Its bird is the Cakravāka. Its two letters are *pa* and *pha*. In this constellation, Hanumān was born. Beyond twenty *ghaṭikās*, there are four poisonous hours (*viṣanāḍyaḥ*). Eating bulbous roots (*kaṃdamūla*) during a journey toward the southwest is auspicious. In cases of fever, there is danger to life. Alternatively, for nine days, there are other portents of misfortune (*ariṣṭa*). For its pacification (*śānti*), the procedure for worshiping the deity Yātudhāna is as follows: Black cloth; black agallochum (*kṛṣṇāgaru*) incense; black lotus flowers; incense of ram’s horn (*meṣaśṛṅga*); and an offering of food with red juice (*raktarasānna*). Having performed the sixteen-fold worship (*ṣoḍaśopacāra*) with the mantra "Moṣuṇaḥ parā," one should offer oblations (*homa*) one hundred and eight times with bulbous roots, fruits, and clarified butter (*ājya*) while reciting the Gāyatrī. One should present offerings of perfumes, garlands, and molasses-rice (*guḍodana*). A black cow should be gifted. After nine days, one becomes well. In this constellation, a woman who experiences her first menstruation becomes a mother of sons. In this constellation, the following are recommended: the *Ṛtupumsavana* (conception rite), *Jātakarman* (birth rites), *Sīmantonnayana* (parting of the hair), naming ceremony (*nāmakaraṇa*), first feeding (*annaprāśana*), beginning of studies (*vidyārambha*), graduation (*samāvartana*), marriage, oil massage (*tailābhyañjana*), wearing gold ornaments, commencement of sacrifices, starting a tree, shaving (*kṣaurakarman*), medical treatment, agriculture, sowing seeds, planting betel-nut trees (*kramuka*), coconut trees, and betel vines (*nāgavallī*), commerce, entering a pond or a cave, exorcising spirits (*bhūtoccāṭana*), application of mantras, and the extraction of yantras. The qualities of one born in this constellation are: a knower of dharma, wealthy, a thief, honorable, affectionate toward kinsmen, red-complexioned, and lustful.
(201) He is prone to illness, fickle, deceitful in action, devoted to discipline, independent, and has a maximum lifespan of ninety-two years; all such details are to be found in this work. || 1 ||
312. Now, regarding the lunar mansion Pūrvāṣāḍhā:
May the deities of Āṣāḍhā always bring auspicious waters that bestow well-being.
The rivers flowing to the ocean are refreshing to all embodied beings.
They are white in color; their presiding deity is Water.
(In the *Nakṣatracūḍāmaṇi*)—
The collection of ponds, tanks, wells, step-wells, oblong pools, corals, pearls, gems, and jewels.
They say that the sharpness of the weapon for unlocking the bolt of the planets resides in the moon when it has entered the water.

**Pūrvāṣāḍhā:** Its seed-syllables are *bu*, *dha*, *bha*, and *ḍha*. Its color is white. It consists of four stars and has the shape of a half-moon. Its gender is female; its source is the monkey (*vānara*); its presiding deity is the Waters (*āpa*); its caste is Brāhmaṇa (*vipra*); its orientation is downward-facing; it possesses four feet; it is fierce (*ugra*); its domain is the intermediate space (*antarikṣa*); it contains half a star; its element is the wind-mandala (*vāyu-maṇḍala*); its location is empty; its tree is the Jambu; its bird is the parrot (*śuka*); its two syllables are *ba* and *bha*. In this asterism, Puṣpadanta was born. The four "poisonous" (*viṣa*) nāḍīs following the twenty-fourth ghaṭikā are to be avoided for journeys. Alternatively, after sixteen ghaṭikās have passed, it is auspicious to drink water or to set out toward the south or west. However, in cases of fever, there is danger to life, or else death within a month. **Rite for its pacification:** Worship of the deity Water (*āp*). White cloth; white Karavīra flowers; incense of realgar (*manaśśilā*); an offering (*naivedya*) of milk-rice. Having worshipped with the sixteen services using the mantra *yat kiṃcid amitam* or *imaṃ me varuṇa*, one should offer oblations one hundred and eight times with red Śāli rice and clarified butter while reciting the Gāyatrī. One should present an oblation (*bali*) of scents, garlands, milk-rice, or *kṛsarānna*. After a month, one becomes well. In this asterism, a woman experiencing her first menstruation becomes husbandless and of ill conduct. In this asterism, the commencement of a courtesan’s profession, the gathering of goods, the planting of sugarcane, the acquisition of letters, hearing, piercing [the ears], the destruction of enemies, and rites such as the *śrāddha* are recommended. The qualities of one born in this asterism: somewhat tall in stature; fine-fingered; devoted to discipline; honored by kings; grasping; famous; having conquered wealth; attached; fond of laughter. His maximum lifespan is ninety years. All such details are to be found in this entire work. (1)

313. Now, regarding the lunar mansion Uttarāṣāḍhā: "I salute all the Viśvedevas, the deities of the Uttarāṣāḍhā mansion, who bestow prosperity, nourishment, fame, and intelligence, for the removal of all sins. (1)
White in color; the Viśvedevas are the presiding deities. — (In the *Nakṣatracūḍāmaṇi*):

One should construct an auspicious temple, a stable dwelling for the installation of the gods, as well as the rites for the worship of the deities and others, propitiatory ceremonies (*śāntika*), festivals, and the consecration of kings.

The erection of pillars, sowing of seeds, planting of creepers, shrubs, and so forth, as well as the demarcation of boundaries, clothing, ornaments, auspicious weddings, and other such matters are to be undertaken under the Viśva-lagna. || 1 ||

**Uttarāṣāḍhā:** The head of an elephant; eight stars; red in color; the form of an elephant's head; feminine gender; belongs to the human class; its source is the *goṣaṇḍa* (cow-pen); the Viśvedevas are its presiding deities; three-footed; facing upward; with wide eyes; the jackfruit tree (*panasa*) is its tree; the Bhāradvāja bird is its bird; stable; its position is empty; the mandala is that of Indra; the seed-syllable is the letter *ma*. A child born under this asterism has four "poisonous" hours (*viṣanāḍī*) after twenty *ghaṭikās*. It is auspicious for eating groats (*saktu*) and for traveling toward the southwest. In cases of fever, there is danger to life, or else death within a month. **For its pacification:** The ritual for worshiping the Viśvedevas involves white cloth, *śrīgandha* (sandalwood paste), flowers of five colors, *uśīra* incense, and an offering of five kinds of edible foods. Having worshipped with the sixteen services (*upacāras*) using the mantra "Viśvedevāsa āgata," one should offer oblations one hundred and eight times with mung-bean rice and clarified butter while reciting the Gāyatrī. One should present an offering of milk-rice along with perfumes and garlands. Within a month, the person becomes well. One should donate a white cow. Under this asterism, a woman experiencing her first menses becomes devoted to her husband and blessed with sons. Under this asterism, the following are recommended: conception during the fertile period (*ṛtu*), the *puṃsavana* rite, the *sīmantonnayana*, naming ceremonies, the first feeding of solid food (*annaprāśana*), ear-piercing, tonsure (*caula*), initiation (*upanayana*), study of the Vedas and Shastras, the return home (*samāvartana*), marriage, oil-massage, anointing with royal unguents, wearing clothes and ornaments, the coronation of kings, the founding and entering of cities and villages, the installation of boundary markers, the planting of seeds for military outposts (*gulma*), the accumulation of wealth and grain, the purchase of fragrant goods, the acquisition of land, and the construction of tanks and other permanent works. The qualities of one born under this asterism are: omniscient, pleasant-minded, of good conduct, broad-hipped, large-eyed, possessed of many virtues, humorous by nature, light in sleep, compassionate, eloquent, righteous, and brave. His maximum lifespan is ninety years. All such details should be understood from this entire treatise. 1.
314. Now, regarding the constellation Abhijit:

"May that which bestows knowledge and sovereignty, which is eternally the state of Brahman devoid of attributes, the Lord of the Abhijit asterism, and the refuge of those who have accomplished the Vedānta, [grant me grace]. (1)
(At this point, only this much remains written in the manuscript)—
p.
203) 315 Now, regarding the asterism Śravaṇa:
He has a peaceful form, four arms, and is the beloved of the Śroṇā constellation.
One should meditate upon Viṣṇu, whose eyes are like lotus petals and who has Garuḍa as his vehicle.
Dark as a blue cloud; Viṣṇu is the deity.
(In the *Nakṣatracūḍāmaṇi*):

One should perform the fire-oblation (*homa*), the initiation for sacrifice (*yajñadīkṣā*), religious observances (*vratas*), the commencement of learning, the tonsure ceremony (*caula*), and the investiture of the sacred thread (*mauñjī-vidhāna*).
The impregnation ceremony, the piercing of the ears, the journey to the abode of Viṣṇu, and the consecration of deities in their shrines.

**Śroṇā (Śravaṇā) Nakṣatra** The three foods are: *śrī*, *śu*, and *śe*. *Śravaṇā*: Black in color; bow-shaped; masculine; belonging to the host of gods (*devagaṇa*); monkey-birth; Viṣṇu as the presiding deity (*devatā*); Brāhmaṇa caste; four-footed; facing upward; beautiful-eyed; moving; internal and external; pertaining to a city; stationary; Indra’s mandala; eight syllables; equal stars; the Arka tree; the Sārasa bird as the vehicle. In this nakṣatra, Aṅgāraka and Vibhīṣaṇa were born. After ten ghaṭikās, there are four poisonous nāḍīs. Eating rice-flour (*śālipiṣṭa*) while traveling toward the southwest is auspicious. In cases of fever, there is danger for eleven days. **Rite for its pacification:** Worship of Viṣṇu according to the prescribed rules. Black cloth; sandalwood, musk, camphor, saffron, and perfumes; Tulasī flowers; ten-ingredient incense (*daśāṅgadhūpa*); an offering of boiled rice (*naivedya*). Having worshipped with the sixteen services (*ṣoḍaśopacāra*) using the mantra "Atodevā" or "Idaṃ viṣṇuḥ," one should offer oblations (*homa*) one hundred and eight times with fuel-sticks of the holy fig tree (*aśvattha*), rice, and clarified butter, reciting the Gāyatrī mantra. One should present offerings of perfumes, garlands, and milk-rice. After eleven days, one becomes well. In this nakṣatra, a woman experiencing her first menses becomes fortunate and possesses sons. In this nakṣatra, the following are recommended: conception (*ṛtu*), the *puṃsavana* rite, the *sīmantonnayana*, naming (*nāmakaraṇa*), the first feeding (*annaprāśana*), ear-piercing, tonsure (*caula*), initiation (*upanayana*), shaving, anointing, learning the alphabet, study of the Vedas and Śāstras, the commencement of new clothes and ornaments, pearls, royal consecration, full-moon festivals, entry into planets, installation of Vaiṣṇava deities, instruction in sacrifices, propitiatory rites (*śāntika*), nourishing rites (*pauṣṭika*), great festivals, practice of mantras, the start of agriculture, sowing seeds, and medical treatments. **Qualities of one born in this nakṣatra:** Black-limbed; robust; wearing variegated garments; fond of incense; devoted to the pleasure of another's wife; noble character; devoted to kinsmen; spending much; fortunate; eloquent; a bad counselor; suffering from diseases such as abdominal tumors (*gulma*); living abroad; fickle; a practitioner of spells; a lord; marked with a fish in the private parts. His maximum lifespan is ninety years. All such details are to be found in this entire work. 1. *Śroṇāhāratrayam* || *Śī śu śe śo śravaṇam* | *Kṛṣṇavarṇaḥ* | *Dhanurākṛtiḥ* | *Pumān* | *Devagaṇaḥ* | *Vānarayoniḥ* | *Viṣṇurdevatā* | *Brāhmaṇajātiḥ* | *Catuṣpāt* | *Ūrdhvamukham* | *Sulocanam* | *Caraḥ* | *Antarbāhyam* | *Pattanam* | *Sthānm* | *Indramaṇḍalam* | *Ṭokṣaraḥ* | *Samatārā* | *Arkavṛkṣaḥ* | *Pakṣīsārasaḥ* || *Asminnakṣatre aṅgārakavibhīṣaṇau jātau* | *Daśaghaṭikābhyaḥ paraṃ viṣanāḍyaścatasraḥ* | *Śālipiṣṭaṃ bhakṣayitvā dakṣiṇapaścimaprayāṇe śubham* | *Jvare ekādaśadinānyariṣṭāni* || — || *Tacchāntyai viṣṇupūjāvidhānam* | *Kṛṣṇavastram* | *Candanakastūrīkarpūrakuṅkumagandhaḥ* | *Tulasīpuṣpam* | *Daśāṅgadhūpaḥ* | *Śālyodananaivedyam* | *Atodevā itimantreṇa idamviṣṇuritimantraṇa vā ṣoḍaśopacāraiḥ saṃpūjya aśvatthasamittandulājyenagāyatryā aṣṭottaraśataṃ juhuyāt* | *Gandhamālyaiḥ kṣīraudanabaliṃ haret* | *Ekādaśāhātsukhī bhavati* || — || *Asminnakṣatre prathamarajasvalā bhāgyaputravatī bhavati* || — || *Asminnakṣatre ṛtupuṃsavanasaumanthanāmakaraṇānnaprāśanakarṇavedhacaulopanayana-kṣaurābhyañjanākṣaragrahaṇavedaśāstrābhyāsanavavastrabhūṣaṇamauktikārambharājābhiṣekapūrṇamāsādigrahapraveśavaiṣṇavadevatāsthāpanayajñopadeśa-śāntikapauṣṭikamahotsavamantābhyāsakṛṣiprārambhabījāvāpanabhaiṣajyādīni-praśastāni* || — || *Asminnakṣatre jātaguṇāḥ* — *Kṛṣṇāṅgaḥ* | *Puṣṭimān* | *Citrāmbaragaḥ* | *Dhapriyaḥ* | *Parasatīratipriyaḥ* | *Udāraśīlaḥ* | *Bandhujanarataḥ* | *Bahuvyayakaraḥ* | *Subhagaḥ* | *Vācakaḥ* | *Durmantrī* | *Gulmādirogī* | *Videśavāsī* | *Capalaḥ* | *Mantravādī* | *Prabhuḥ* | *Guhyadeśematsyāṅkitaḥ* || *Navativarṣāṇi paramāyurityādikaṃ sarvamasmingranthe draṣṭavyam* || 1 ||
316. Now, regarding the lunar mansion Dhaniṣṭhā:
[one should worship] those who have taken refuge in the deities of Śraviṣṭhā, Vaṃdeva, and Sūnu.
Their hands were marked with conchs and discs, and their heads were adorned with crowns.
White in color; the Vasus are the presiding deities. — (In the *Nakṣatracūḍāmaṇi*):
Knowledge, sacred scriptures, the initiation ceremony (*upanayana*), collyrium, medicines, white parasols, beds, seats, and food.

Sacrifices, consecrations, auspicious rites, pacifying ceremonies, nourishing rites, and the construction of palaces and cities are accomplished when the asterism of Vāsava (Dhruva) is in the ascendant. || 1 ||

Dhaniṣṭhā has the shape of a mṛdaṅga drum; its four stars are *gā*, *gī*, *gū*, and *ge*. It is white in color, consists of four stars, and is shaped like a mṛdaṅga. Its gender is feminine. The Rākṣasa class of beings presides over it; its source (*yoni*) is the lioness (*siṃhī*). The Vasus are its deities; its livelihood is the artisan class (*upajīvijāti*). Its face is turned upward, and its eyes are blind. Its location is the intermediate space (*antarikṣa*), and its place is the village. Its mandala is that of Indra; its tree is the *śamī*; its bird is the bee. It consists of three syllables. A person born under this asterism is born with the sound of a drum. Beyond ten *ghaṭikās* [from birth], there are four poisonous *nāḍīs*. Traveling toward the east or north after consuming sesame and rice is auspicious. In case of fever, there is danger for one month. For its pacification, the following ritual for worshiping the auspicious deity is prescribed: white cloth, sandalwood paste, *śatapatra* flowers, *guggulu* incense, and milk-rice (*pāyasa*) as an offering. Having performed the sixteen-fold worship (*ṣoḍaśopacāra-pūjā*) with the mantra "Trātāram" (Rig Veda 1.98.1), one should offer oblations (*homa*) one hundred and eight times with *audumbara* wood fuel and clarified butter while reciting the Gāyatrī mantra. One should present offerings of perfumes, garlands, and milk-rice. After one month, the person becomes well. Under this asterism, a woman experiencing her first menstrual period will bear a son. Under this asterism, the following are recommended: sexual union, naming ceremonies, the first feeding of solid food (*annaprāśana*), ear-piercing, tonsure (*caula*), initiation (*upanayana*), oil massage, wearing clothes and ornaments, mounting the fourfold army, using swings, umbrellas, and chowries, service to deities, commencement of enterprises, journeys, entries, propitiatory rites (*śāntika*), nourishing rites (*pauṣṭika*), great festivals, dance, song, instrumental music, the start of agriculture, sowing seeds, training elephants and other animals, buying and selling, and so forth. The qualities of one born under this asterism are: knowing little of the scriptures, radiant, industrious, having a stout body, fond of dance, song, and women, humble, a speaker of falsehood, a servant of the king, an alchemist (*dhātuvādī*), devoid of compassion, a doer of evil deeds, having a hot body, slanderous, and a maximum lifespan of seventy-five years. All such details are to be found in this entire treatise. 1.
317. Now, regarding the lunar mansion Śatabhiṣaj: I constantly revere Varuṇa, the deity of Śatabhiṣaj, who holds a jar of nectar, carries a noose in his hand, and is praised by the gods. (1)
Golden-hued; Varuṇa is the presiding deity. — (In the Nakṣatracūḍāmaṇi).
The management of reservoirs, gardens, and agriculture, as well as the collection of coral, pearls, and other such items.
One should perform the pacification of horses through recitation, fire-oblations, and gifts; and during the Śata-tārakā constellation, one should apply eye-salve.

Śatabhiṣak (the Hundred Stars) consists of one hundred stars. Its shape is circular. Its seed-syllables are *go*, *sā*, *sī*, *sū*, and *śatabhiṣak*. Its color is red. It has the form of a shower of flowers. It is neuter. Its presiding group is the Rākṣasas. Its source is the horse (*turagī*). Varuṇa is its deity. It belongs to the Kṣatriya caste. Its face is upward-facing. Its eyes are round. It is the last (of the lunar mansions). It is at the end. Its stars are equal in number. Its position is empty. Its mandala is that of Varuṇa. Its tree is the Kadamba. Its bird is the cuckoo. Its letter is the syllable *ṣa*. Varuṇa was born under this asterism. Beyond eighteen *ghaṭikās* (forty-eight minutes), there are four poisonous *nāḍīs*. Eating rice under this asterism is auspicious for a journey toward the east or north. In case of fever, there is danger to life; otherwise, there are eleven days of misfortune. For its pacification, the ritual for the worship of Varuṇa is as follows: white cloth, a hundred-petaled lotus flower, sandalwood paste, camphor incense, and an offering of food with ghee. Having worshipped with the sixteen services using the mantra "Avate heḍa," one should offer oblations one hundred and eight times with water-born flowers and clarified butter while reciting the Gāyatrī. One should present offerings of perfumes, garlands, and milk-rice. After eleven days, one becomes well. Under this asterism, a woman experiencing her first menses will have a son and will possess some degree of anger. Under this asterism, the following auspicious activities are recommended: sexual union, naming ceremonies, the first feeding of solid food, the tonsure ceremony, the initiation into sacred study (*upanayana*), learning the alphabet, the study of the Vedas and Shastras, oil massages, the coronation of kings, the acquisition of elephants, horses, and pearls, the application of collyrium to the eyes, the installation of deities, the construction of bridges, the commencement of waterworks, the adoption of a son, commerce, buying and selling, agriculture, the application of business methods, and the sowing of seeds. The qualities of one born under this asterism are: large-bodied, honored by the world, having many sons, a benefactor to his circle of relatives, a slayer of enemies, long-lived, engaged in trade, afflicted by blood-related diseases, possessing the qualities of a rogue, possessing some knowledge, fickle, talkative, dark-complexioned, brave, firm-minded, a father of excellent sons, an enemy of moral conduct, possessing little learning, and extremely arrogant. His maximum lifespan is eighty years. These and other details should be observed in this work. 1.
318. Now, regarding the lunar mansion Pūrvābhādrapadā:
With my head, I salute Ajaikapād, the dispeller of darkness, the lord of Proṣṭhapada, who is honored by all the gods. (1)
Red in color; the deity is Ajaikapād. (In the *Nakṣatracūḍāmaṇi*):
[It grants] the commencement of learning, the binding of elephants, the possession by Vetālas and others, and the power of ritual formulas (*kalpavāda*).
One should undertake gambling, set out on a journey, and practice the study of the scriptures when the Moon is in a single-footed sign. || 1 ||

Pūrvābhādrapadā and Uttarābhādrapadā are each four-cornered. Pūrvābhādrapadā is represented by the letter *se*, has a black color, consists of two stars, is three-legged, shaped like a bedstead (*khaṭvā*), is masculine, belongs to the human class, has the lion as its source, has Ajaikapād as its presiding deity, is of the Brāhmaṇa caste, faces downward, has eyes in the middle, is fierce, is internal, has equal stars, its location is a city, its mandala is that of Indra, its tree is the mango (*cūta*), its bird is the dove, and its syllable is *la*. A Kinnara is born under this asterism. After sixteen *ghaṭikās*, there are four poisonous *nāḍīs* (hours) which must be avoided for a journey. Alternatively, it is auspicious for a departure toward the east or north after drinking honey. In case of fever, there is danger to life, or else death within a month. For its pacification, the procedure for the worship of the deity Ajaikapād is as follows: red cloth, saffron-scented paste, *arka* flowers, incense of ten medicinal herbs, and an offering of curd-rice (*dadhyodana*). Having worshipped with the sixteen services using the mantra "Śam agniḥ," one should offer one hundred and eight oblations of food and clarified butter with the *Gāyatrī* mantra, and present an offering of milk-rice with perfumes and garlands. One becomes happy after a month. Under this asterism, a woman experiences her first menses or becomes a widow. Under this asterism, cruel activities such as beginning studies, seizing a village, sorcery, theft, strife, gambling, legal disputes, imprisonment, digging wells, tanks, or ponds, entering great caverns, sowing dissension among enemies, the employment of mantras against spirits, ghosts, and demons, eradication (*uccāṭana*), alchemy (*dhātuvāda*), and so forth, are recommended. The qualities of one born under this asterism are: lotus-eyed, wealthy, very generous, fond of women, charitable by nature, fortunate, composed in appearance, famous, very irascible, long-lived, possessing great happiness and wealth, suffering from throat ailments, free from the afflictions of hunger and thirst, and having a maximum lifespan of ninety-six years. All such details are to be found in this entire treatise. 1.
319. Now, concerning the lunar mansion Uttarābhādrapadā: May the Lord of the Proṣṭhapadas, Ahirbudhnya, be for our great joy.
His hands were marked with the conch and the discus, and his head was radiant with a crown.
White in color; Ahibudhnya is the presiding deity. — (In the Nakṣatracūḍāmaṇi):
Stable rites, nourishing ceremonies, auspicious acts, marriages, sacrifices, and other such undertakings [are to be performed under this asterism].
When the moon has entered the asterism of Ahibudhnya, the consecration of kings, as well as garments and ornaments, attain success. || 1 ||
Pūrvābhādrapadā and Uttarābhādrapadā each consist of two [stars] and form a square.

**Duḥśaṃḍā** (Uttarābhādrapadā): White in color; two stars; shaped like a sword; masculine; belongs to the human class; cow-born; Ahirbudhnya is its presiding deity; of the Kṣatriya caste; facing upward; beautiful-eyed; four-footed; its stars are equal in number; two syllables, *halau*; its place is the village; its element is air (*vāyu*); its tree is the *picunada*; its bird is the cuckoo.
